news.head: Rico Dowdle (toe) officially active for Week 6
news.impact: Dowdle has dealt with a toe injury that has kept him sidelined since Week 2. Jaylen Warren will likely still see the bulk of the carries, but Dowdle's return will result in less work for Warren.

news.body: Rico Dowdle (toe) is officially questionable for Sunday's game against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.
news.head: Rico Dowdle (toe) officially questionable for Sunday
news.impact: Dowdle may be available to make his return to the lineup on Sunday after logging two full practices to end the week, but he is still questionable, so that is uncertain at this point. His return would mean a but less work for Jaylen Warren moving forward, although Dowdle himself would be unlikely to have standalone value.

news.body: Rico Dowdle (toe) was upgraded to a full participant at practice on Thursday.
news.head: Rico Dowdle (toe) upgraded to full participant Thursday
news.impact: The veteran running back was able to practice in a full capacity on Thursday after being limited by a toe injury on Wednesday. He should be available to play in Week 6 and will likely be an involved RB2 for the Steelers behind Jaylen Warren moving forward.

news.body: RJ Harvey ran six times for 25 yards and a touchdown while also catching three of four targets for 31 yards in the Broncos' 17-14 win over Seattle on Thursday.
news.head: RJ Harvey bounces back in Thursday win
news.impact: After going silent in Week 5, Harvey got back on track in Week 6, scoring a touchdown and even leading the Broncos in receiving. That last bit is a huge indictment of the Broncos' passing game, which has struggled mightily this year. Harvey is an RB3 at best right now, but if you have other options with a more stable floor who can start, that's likely the best course of action.

news.body: RJ Harvey gained seven yards on three carries and failed to catch his only target in Sunday's 23-17 win over the Chargers.
news.head: RJ Harvey a non-factor in Week 5 win
news.impact: A week after coming up with 10 catches, Harvey was blanked in the passing game and limited to just three touches Sunday afternoon. J.K. Dobbins shouldered the load out of the backfield in this victory, making it clear that Harvey is still firmly behind him on the depth chart. Harvey is a worthwhile handcuff to stash, but he is game-script dependent and unreliable as long as Dobbins remains healthy.

news.body: J.K. Dobbins rushed 11 times for 40 yards, while RJ Harvey had seven carries for 25 yards in Sunday's 24-14 loss to the San Francisco 49ers. Harvey also caught 10 passes for 68 yards out of the backfield.
news.head: RJ Harvey, J.K. Dobbins struggle in loss Sunday
news.impact: Denver couldn't get much going on the ground, with Dobbins and Harvey combining for just 65 rushing yards. Dobbins continued to handle more of the rushing work, but Harvey was much more involved as a receiver and ended up leading the Broncos in both receptions and receiving yards. The backfield remains a split, with Dobbins having the better chance at early-down work and Harvey carrying more upside in the passing game.

news.body: RJ Harvey is off the injury report on Wednesday.
news.head: RJ Harvey (concussion) off injury report
news.impact: Harvey was checked for a concussion in Week. He will be good to go in his complimentary role next to J.K. Dobbins.

news.body: Roschon Johnson carried the ball 13 times for a team-high 51 yards and one touchdown while also catching both of his targets for 34 yards in the Bears' 31-23 Week 6 win over the Atlanta Falcons.
news.head: Roschon Johnson leads backfield in Week 6 win
news.impact: Johnson made the most of increased touches in the Chicago offense, finishing with over 40 offensive yards for the first time this season. The running back remains more of a handcuff option as part of a Chicago backfield led by D'Andre Swift and missing Kyle Monangai, with a Week 7 matchup against the New England Patriots up next.

news.body: Roschon Johnson rushed five times for six yards while also catching five of his seven targets for 34 yards in the Bears' 31-7 loss to the Green Bay Packers in Week 5.
news.head: Roschon Johnson sees 10 touches in Week 5 loss
news.impact: Johnson has seen increased involvement out of the Chicago backfield of late, recording five or more touches in each of the last two games. The running back remains difficult to trust when the Chicago backfield is fully healthy, with a Week 6 contest against the Atlanta Falcons up next.

news.body: Roschon Johnson (back) was limited at practice again on Thursday.
news.head: Roschon Johnson (back) limited again Thursday
news.impact: Johnson was able to practice for a second-straight day on Thursday. He remained limited due to a back issue, but he still seems to be trending the right way for Week 10. His return would mean slightly less work for rookie Kyle Monangai moving forward.

news.body: Roschon Johnson (back) was limited at practice on Wednesday.
news.head: Roschon Johnson (back) limited Wednesday
news.impact: Johnson has been sidelined for the past couple of weeks due to a back injury, but he was able to practice in a limited fashion on Wednesday and seems to trending the right way for Sunday's game. Rookie Kyle Monangai will see a slight decrease in work if Johnson is back in the lineup this week.

news.body: Saquon Barkley has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Panthers.
news.head: Saquon Barkley (hamstring) ruled out Sunday
news.impact: Barkley will remain sidelined after not practicing all week. Dameon Pierce is in line to lead the Eagles backfield.

news.body: Saquon Barkley (hamstring) is not at practice on Thursday. Yet another absence for the talented running back.
news.head: Saquon Barkley (hamstring) not at practice Thursday
news.impact: The Eagles are in dire straights at running back right now, with Dameon Pierce, the team’s RB4, as their top option. They’re also down Jalen Hurts, who will miss this week due to a blood clot, and DeVonta Smith also missed practice. Saquon will have to put in some sort of work on Friday to have much hope of playing this weekend.

news.body: Saquon Barkley did not practice on Wednesday.
news.head: Saquon Barkley (hamstring) misses practice Wednesday
news.impact: Barkley is continuing to work his way ban from a hamstring injury. His status is uncertain for Sunday's game against the Panthers.

news.body: Saquon Barkley was not at practice on Wednesday.
news.head: Saquon Barkley (hamstring) not at practice Wednesday
news.impact: Barkley remains hopeful to return for Sunday's game against the Panthers. His status will need to be monitored in practice the next couple of days.

news.body: Seth McGowan ran four times for 27 yards in the Colts' 26-20 loss to the Titans on Sunday.
news.head: Seth McGowan runs for 27 yards in loss
news.impact: McGowan is once again playing backup to Jonathan Taylor, which is unlikely to change. Keep him stashed on your bench if you have Taylor.

news.body: Seth McGowan ran five times for 16 yards and caught his only target for three yards in the Colts' 34-22 loss to the Steelers on Sunday.
news.head: Seth McGowan sees six touches in loss
news.impact: McGowan was the clear No.2 back behind Jonathan Taylor yet again, but it didn't amount to much for fantasy. He's a clear-cut handcuff and not a bad one to have, but it's unlikely he will garner enough of a workload to really warrant starting him without a Taylor injury.

news.body: Seth McGowan caught his only target for no gain in the Colts' 41-23 loss to the Baltimore Ravens in Week 1.
news.head: Seth McGowan catches one pass in Week 1
news.impact: McGowan was one of many options in the Indianapolis offense that failed to make an impact in the Week 1 loss and can remain off rosters in all formats ahead of a tough Week 2 contest against the Kansas City Chiefs.

news.body: The Indianapolis Colts have selected RB Seth McGowan with the No. 237 overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft.
news.head: Seth McGowan selected No. 237 by Indianapolis Colts
news.impact: McGowan is a tough, physical runner who keeps his legs moving through contact. He can catch passes out of the backfield - though not the strongest area of his game - but, he is good in pass protection and is willing to block would-be pass rushers. McGowan ran for 725 yards and 12 touchdowns at Kentucky in 2025 and joins the Colts to compete for a backup role to Jonathan Taylor in Indianapolis.

news.body: Sione Vaki rushed the ball one time for seven yards and caught one pass for 13 yards in Thursday's 41-31 loss to the Buffalo Bills.
news.head: Sione Vaki uninvolved in loss Thursday
news.impact: Vaki continues to make minimal impact on Detroit's offense. He has squarely established himself as the RB2 behind Jahmyr Gibbs, but that role hasn't furnished him with many opportunities over the first two weeks of the season. He remains nothing more than a mid-tier handcuff option for the foreseeable future.

news.body: Sione Vaki caught his only target for 11 yards while also rushing twice for seven yards in the Lions' 31-30 win over the New Orleans Saints in Week 1.
news.head: Sione Vaki sees three touches in Week 1
news.impact: Vaki was an afterthought out of the backfield, being out-carried by Jahmyr Gibbs 29-2 in the win. The running back remains little more than an underwhelming handcuff to Gibbs ahead of a Week 2 contest against the Buffalo Bills.

news.body: Sione Vaki (thumb) remained limited for another practice session on Wednesday.
news.head: Sione Vaki (thumb) remains limited Wednesday
news.impact: Vaki has been dealing with this thumb injury for a while already and will remain limited for another practice on Wednesday as a result. He remains off of the fantasy radar at this point in the season, however, so fantasy managers shouldn't read much into his availability for Sunday's game.

news.body: Sione Vaki (thumb) was limited at practice again on Wednesday.
news.head: Sione Vaki (thumb) limited again Wednesday
news.impact: Vaki has been managing this thumb injury for a little while and was limited at another practice on Wednesday because of it. It remains to be seen whether or not it will leave him with an injury designation for Week 15, but either way fantasy managers shouldn't put much weight into his status.

news.body: Tony Pollard ran 19 times for 76 yards in the Titans' 26-20 win over the Colts. He failed to bring in his only target.
news.head: Tony Pollard runs for 76 yards in win
news.impact: Pollard had the backfield virtually all to himself, aside from Tyjae Spears getting a single carry. A touchdown or some receiving work would have helped Pollard's bottom line tremendously, but it was not meant to be. If anything, his volume seems to be solid, so he's an RB3 with upside.

news.body: Tony Pollard (rest) returned to practice as a full participant on Thursday.
news.head: Tony Pollard (rest) returns to practice Thursday
news.impact: Pollard was given the day off on Wednesday as a veteran rest day, and he was able to make his return to practice as a full participant on Thursday. He should be good to go for Week 6 and will be primed for more work than usual if Tyjae Spears (knee) is limited or sidelined against the Colts on Sunday.

news.body: Tony Pollard (rest) was absent from Tennessee's practice on Wednesday.
news.head: Tony Pollard (rest) absent from practice Wednesday
news.impact: Pollard was given the day off on Wednesday as a veteran rest day. He should be back at practice on Thursday and is expected to be fully healthy for Week 6, assuming nothing happens throughout the week.

news.body: Tony Pollard ran for 52 yards on 14 carries in the Titans 26-3 loss against the Texans.
news.head: Tony Pollard rushes for 52 yards Sunday
news.impact: Pollard did not catch his lone target and didn't rip off longer than a 14-yard run. He'll remain a desperate RB2 play next week against the Colts.

news.body: TreVeyon Henderson rushed for 31 yards on seven carries in the 26-19 win over the Jets. He caught his lone target for nine yards.
news.head: TreVeyon Henderson logs eight touches in Week 6 win
news.impact: Henderson returned from a high-ankle sprain that he suffered last week, but saw Corey Kiner run the ball more Sunday. Henderson did fumble the ball to the Jets, which likely impacted his playing time late in the game. Henderson and the Patriots will take on the Bears in Week 7.

news.body: Patriots RB TreVeyon Henderson (ankle) is officially active for a Week 6 matchup with the Jets.
news.head: TreVeyon Henderson (ankle) officially active for Week 6
news.impact: Henderson was listed as questionable due to a high-ankle sprain he suffered last week. Even with Henderson active, Rhamondre Stevenson will likely see the bulk of the carries for the Patriots against the Jets.

news.body: TreVeyon Henderson (ankle) is questionable for Sunday's game against the New York Jets.
news.head: TreVeyon Henderson (ankle) questionable for Sunday
news.impact: Henderson suffered a high-ankle sprain last week, but he may not have to miss any time because of it, as he is officially considered questionable to play in Week 6. Fantasy managers shouldn't trust starting him even if he's active, however, and Rhamondre Stevenson will be a quality starting option if the young running back is ruled out against the Jets.

news.body: TreVeyon Henderson was at practice again on Friday.
news.head: TreVeyon Henderson (ankle) practicing Friday
news.impact: Henderson was limited in practice again on Thursday. It was seeming like he would be sidelined this week after suffering a high-ankle sprain, but he has practiced all week. He'll need to be monitored on the official injury report.

news.body: Ty Johnson (hamstring) was a limited participant at practice on Thursday.
news.head: Ty Johnson (hamstring) limited participant Thursday
news.impact: Johnson was able to practice on Thursday, though he was limited by a hamstring injury again. It seems likely that he will be active and continue to play a depth role for the Bills again in Week 6.

news.body: Ty Johnson (hamstring) was limited at practice on Wednesday.
news.head: Ty Johnson (hamstring) limited Wednesday
news.impact: Johnson was left limited at practice on Wednesday due to a hamstring injury that he's still managing. It shouldn't affect his availability for Week 6, however, unless he suffers a setback at some point in the week.

news.body: Ty Johnson caught all four of his targets for 72 yards in a 37-34 overtime win over the Rams in Week 5's Monday night game.
news.head: Ty Johnson goes for 72 receiving yards in Week 5
news.impact: Johnson didn't see a carry in the contest but he finished second on the Bills in receiving yards in the exciting win. The veteran running back continues to be a threat in the passing attack as this was his second game this season with at least 50 receiving yards. Johnson will now prepare to take on the Raiders in Week 6.

news.body: Ty Johnson rushed for three yards on one carry in the loss to the Patriots. He caught both of his targets for nine yards.
news.head: Ty Johnson sees three touches in Week 4
news.impact: Johnson continues to operate as the change of pace back, but has limited fantasy value right now. Fantasy managers can leave Johnson on the waiver wire heading into a matchup with the Rams.

news.body: Tyjae Spears ran once for a yard and caught his only target for three yards in the Titans' 26-20 win over Indianapolis on Sunday.
news.head: Tyjae Spears quiet in win over Colts
news.impact: A week after catching nine passes, Spears was nearly wiped out of the game plan for Tennessee. It's tough to trust Spears moving forward, and he's best left on waivers.

news.body: Titans RB Tyjae Spears (knee) is officially active for a Week 6 matchup with the Colts.
news.head: Tyjae Spears (knee) officially active for Week 6
news.impact: Spears was considered questionable to play as he continues to deal with a minor knee injury. Fantasy managers should expect both Spears and Tony Pollard to be involved in the Titans' backfield.

news.body: Tyjae Spears (knee) is questionable for Sunday's game against the Indianapolis Colts.
news.head: Tyjae Spears (knee) questionable for Sunday
news.impact: Spears is uncertain to play on Sunday. He is managing a nagging knee issue of some kind right now, but he was able to log a full practice on Friday still, which is a good sign that he will play through it. He will be worth keeping an eye on in this matchup if active, as he saw high involvement in the team's passing game last week.

news.body: Tyjae Spears (knee) was downgraded to a non-participant at practice on Thursday.
news.head: Tyjae Spears (knee) downgraded to non-participant Thursday
news.impact: Spears was limited at Wednesday's practice due to a knee issue, but he was downgraded to a non-participant on Thursday. It's still unclear if this was simply a load management move on the part of the team or if this is a real issue for him, so fantasy managers should keep close tabs on his status heading into the weekend and expect more work for Tony Pollard if Spears is ruled out for Week 6.

news.body: Tyler Allgeier rushed the ball three times for seven yards and caught two passes for nine yards in Sunday's 45-21 loss to the Detroit Lions.
news.head: Tyler Allgeier quiet in loss Sunday
news.impact: Allgeier wasn't able to do much on Sunday. He logged just 16 total yards on his five touches, and he wasn't able to get into the end zone at all, which left him with a terrible fantasy total. He is unlikely to be fantasy relevant moving forward, besides being a handcuff option behind rookie Jeremiyah Love.

news.body: Tyler Allgeier rushed the ball eight times for 42 yards and a touchdown while catching two passes for seven yards through the air in Sunday's 36-24 loss to the New York Giants.
news.head: Tyler Allgeier finds end zone Sunday
news.impact: The veteran was able to contribute on Sunday, finishing with 49 total yards and a touchdown in the team's loss to the Giants. It seems like rookie Jeremiyah Love is dealing with some bumps and bruises right now too, so Allgeier could see more work in the future if the rookie is limited by that at all.

news.body: Tyler Allgeier ran for -1 yard on two carries in the Cardinals 36-30 loss against the 49ers on Sunday. He also caught 4-of-4 targets for 10 yards receiving.
news.head: Tyler Allgeier has quiet day Sunday
news.impact: Allgeier took a step back to rookie RB Jeremiyah Love for the first time this season on the day. If this trend continues, he'll remain a pure stash for fantasy managers.

news.body: Tyler Allgeier ran five times for 10 yards and caught both of his targets for 9 yards in the Cardinals' 31-7 loss to the Seahawks on Sunday.
news.head: Tyler Allgeier gets seven touches in loss
news.impact: Allgeier played second fiddle to Jeremiyah Love on Sunday, which is to be expected. He wasn't particularly efficient on his limited work, but no one in the offense really got going anyway. It was tough sledding for the veteran, but hopefully things will get a little easier against San Fransisco next Sunday.

news.body: Woody Marks rushed for 56 yards on 15 carries in the Texans' 34-31 win over the Jaguars. He caught 2-of-3 targets for 25 yards.
news.head: Woody Marks sees 17 touches in Week 6 win
news.impact: Marks led the running back room in touches, but did see Jawhar Jordan score the lone rushing touchdown for Houston. Fantasy managers should expect Marks and Jordan to continue to get work if David Montgomery (groin) is forced to miss more time.

news.body: Woody Marks will reportedly "carry the load" for the Texans with David Montgomery week-to-week with a groin injury.
news.head: Woody Marks will 'carry the load' for Texans with Montgomery out
news.impact: Marks had 19 touches on Sunday and he operated as the Texans lead back in 2025, so this is nothing new to him. He's not overly dynamic, despite the coachspeak, but he can get it done for fantasy thanks to volume. He's a low-end RB2, high-end RB3 with the backfield to himself.

news.body: Woody Marks ran for 62 yards on 15 carries in the Texans 26-3 win over the Titans. He also caught 4-of-4 targets for 23 yards receiving.
news.head: Woody Marks sees 19 touches Sunday
news.impact: Marks was the lead back for Houston most of the afternoon after David Montgomery injured his groin and did not return. He had a 20 yard touchdown taken off the board due to a holding penalty. He'll be an RB2 play next week against the Jaguars.

news.body: Woody Marks ran for 22 yards on six carries and a touchdown in the Texans 34-30 loss against the Cowboys.
news.head: Woody Marks scores again Sunday
news.impact: Marks continues to play a role in the Texans backfield next to David Montgomery. Neither of them got much going on the ground. He'll be an upside flex play next week against the Titans.

news.body: Zach Charbonnet has been ruled out for Thursday’s game against the Broncos.
news.head: Zach Charbonnet (knee) ruled out for Thursday
news.impact: Charbonnet remains hopeful to make his season debut next week against the Chiefs.

news.body: Zach Charbonnet has a “legitimate chance” to play in Week 7 against the Chiefs.
news.head: Zach Charbonnet (knee) has 'legitimate chance' to return in Week 7
news.impact: This was the expectation with the Seahawks having a mini bye following the team playing on Thursday this week. He'll likely be eased back, but the Seahawks need him back more than ever right now given the struggles with the run game.

news.body: Seahawks coach Mike Macdonald said he does not plan to play Zach Charbonnet in Week 6 against the Broncos.
news.head: Zach Charbonnet (knee) not expected to return in Week 6
news.impact: That was the expectation with it being a short week for Seattle. Charbonnet should return in Week 7 against the Chiefs. It will be one more game of Emanuel Wilson leading the Seahawks backfield on Thursday against the Broncos.

news.body: Seahawks coach Mike Macdonald said Seattle’s Week 6 Thursday Night Football game against the Broncos makes Zach Charbonnet’s ramp-up “tricky.”
news.head: Zach Charbonnet (knee) uncertain for Week 6
news.impact: Charbonnet has been limited since returning to practice, but a short week in Week 6 makes a return then tricky. It sounds like Week 7 against the Chiefs is more likely when he returns.

news.body: AJ Barner caught three of four targets for 16 yards in the Seahawks' 17-14 loss to the Broncos on Thursday.
news.head: AJ Barner catches three passes in loss
news.impact: Barner hasn't really gotten going this season after showing a lot of promise in 2025. The ability is there; we saw it back in Week 3 against Washington, but the opportunity hasn't been. He's not startable in fantasy right now.

news.body: AJ Barner caught 3-of-5 targets for 20 yards in the Seahawks 32-29 loss against the 49ers.
news.head: AJ Barner catches three passes Sunday
news.impact: Barner remains off the fantasy radar in his current role.

news.body: AJ Barner caught 1-of-3 targets for 12 yards in the Seahawks 30-23 win over the Chargers.
news.head: AJ Barner quiet Sunday
news.impact: Barner was coming off a big performance last week. He remains a volatile TE2 for fantasy managers.

news.body: AJ Barner caught five of his nine targets for 69 yards in the Seahawks’ 33-31 Week 3 loss to the Washington Commanders.
news.head: AJ Barner catches five passes in Week 3 loss
news.impact: Barner has seen minimal involvement in the Seattle passing attack early on, recording more than two receptions for the first time in three contests Sunday. The tight end remains difficult to trust ahead of a Week 4 contest against the Los Angeles Chargers.

news.body: Brenton Strange caught 5-of-7 targets for 44 yards in the 34-31 loss to the Texans.
news.head: Brenton Strange catches five passes in Week 6 loss
news.impact: Strange continues to lead the tight end group for the Jaguars. The 25-year-old has logged three straight games with at least five receptions. Strange and the Jaguars will head to the bye in Week 7.

news.body: Brenton Strange secured 7-of-8 targets for 68 yards in Sunday's 19-17 win over the Eagles.
news.head: Brenton Strange leads Jaguars in catches for second straight week
news.impact: Strange has now come up with seven receptions in two straight games, leading all Jaguars both times. He's hauled in 14 of 16 passes overall in that span, gaining 163 yards in the process. Strange has not found the end zone since Week 1, but he has been close a couple of times, including in this win against the Eagles. He's rapidly climbing up the TE ranks in his fourth NFL season.

news.body: Brenton Strange hauled in 7-of-8 targets for 95 yards in Sunday's 22-17 win over the Cincinnati Bengals.
news.head: Brenton Strange leads team in receiving Sunday
news.impact: The veteran tight end stepped up on Sunday. He finished as the team's top receiver with 95 yards against the Bengals, which was very timely on an afternoon where most of their receiving options were struggling. He had a good fantasy total in this game, but managers shouldn't expect this to be a regular thing for him moving forward.

news.body: Brenton Strange caught 3-of-5 targets for 32 yards in Sunday's 35-6 blowout win over the New England Patriots.
news.head: Brenton Strange catches three passes Sunday
news.impact: Strange was a solid contributor for the Jaguars on Sunday, hauling in three passes en route to a big win over the Patriots. Still, he isn't a strong fantasy option and shouldn't be considered startable for the foreseeable future.

news.body: Brock Bowers (knee) practiced in a full capacity on Thursday.
news.head: Brock Bowers (knee) practices in full Thursday
news.impact: Bowers was upgraded to a full participant at practice on Thursday after being limited by his knee injury on Wednesday. He should be fully good to go for Week 6 and remains a must-start fantasy option moving forward.

news.body: Brock Bowers (knee) was limited at practice on Wednesday.
news.head: Brock Bowers (knee) limited at practice Wednesday
news.impact: Bowers was limited at Wednesday's practice, which doesn't come as a surprise, as the team has made a habit out of limiting his workload early in the week. He should be available to play in Week 6 and will remain a top-tier fantasy option moving forward.

news.body: Brock Bowers caught 8-of-10 targets for 110 yards and a touchdown in the Raiders loss to the Patriots.
news.head: Brock Bowers eclipses 100 yards in Week 5 loss
news.impact: Bowers has now caught a touchdown in all three games he has appeared in this season, and logged double digit targets in each contest as well. Bowers will look to continue an excellent start to his season in Week 6 against Buffalo.

news.body: Brock Bowers (knee) was limited at practice on Wednesday.
news.head: Brock Bowers (knee) limited at practice Wednesday
news.impact: Bowers was a limited participant at practice on Wednesday. This is likely just a load management move on the part of the team early on in the practice week, so fantasy managers should have no concerns about his outlook for Week 5 unless he's downgraded at some point this week.

news.body: Cade Otton caught three of four targets for 25 yards in the Bucs' 24-16 win over the Cowboys on Thursday.
news.head: Cade Otton catches three passes in win
news.impact: Otton had two of his three catches on the first drive, and wasn't heard from much afterwards. The passing offense under Jaylon Daniels is still effective, just not explosive. Things get done, but maybe not in a fantasy-friendly manner. That's going to hurt Otton's fantasy value until something changes.

news.body: Cade Otton caught four of his six targets for 37 yards in a 17-14 loss to the Packers in Week 4.
news.head: Cade Otton leads Bucs in receiving in Week 4
news.impact: Otton was busy in quarterback Jalon Daniels' NFL debut, serving as a safety valve for the rookie. The veteran tight end has drawn exactly six targets in three straight games for Tampa. Overall, he has 15 catches for 157 yards through four games. He will be a low-end TE2 in Week 5 vs. the Cowboys.

news.body: Cade Otton caught 3-of-6 targets for 56 yards in the Buccaneers 23-16 loss against the Vikings on Sunday.
news.head: Cade Otton a safety blanket for the Buccaneers Sunday
news.impact: Otton was second on the team in targets on the day. He has seen at least five targets in all three weeks to start the season. He'll remain a high floor tight end play next week against the Packers.

news.body: Cade Otton caught 5-of-6 targets for 38 yards in the Buccaneers 23-19 loss against the Browns.
news.head: Cade Otton catches five passes Sunday
news.impact: Otton was a safety blanket all afternoon for Baker Mayfield. He remains a TE2 for fantasy managers.

news.body: Chig Okonkwo caught four of his team-high six targets for 60 yards in the Commanders' 27-27 Week 5 tie with the New York Giants.
news.head: Chig Okonkwo catches four passes in Week 5 tie
news.impact: Okonkwo was impactful in the rain-soaked Week 5 contest for head coach Dan Quinn, recording over 50 receiving yards for the first time in his three contests. The tight end remains another risky pass-catching option in all formats ahead of a Week 6 contest against the San Francisco 49ers.

news.body: Chig Okonkwo (hamstring) was listed as a limited participant at practice on Thursday.
news.head: Chig Okonkwo (hamstring) listed as limited Thursday
news.impact: The veteran tight end was able to log another limited practice session on Thursday. His hamstring injury isn't serious at this point, however, and he is expected to play through it in this week's matchup against the Giants.

news.body: Chig Okonkwo (hamstring) was listed as a limited participant at practice on Wednesday.
news.head: Chig Okonkwo (hamstring) listed as limited Wednesday
news.impact: Okonkwo was able to make his return to the lineup in Week 4 after missing a bit of time due to a hamstring injury. It's not surprising that the team continues to limit his workload at practice because of it, but he still should be good to play through it in Week 5, assuming he doesn't re-aggravate the injury sometime during the week.

news.body: Chig Onkonkwo (hamstring) will play Sunday.
news.head: Chig Okonkwo (hamstring) to return Sunday
news.impact: Okonkwo has been out since Week 1 due to a hamstring injury, but after getting in limited practice sessions this week, he is ready to return to action this Sunday. Okonkwo hauled in 2-of-3 targets for 16 yards in the Commanders' 24-22 loss to the Eagles in Week 1.

news.body: Dallas Goedert caught 6-of-9 targets for 38 yards in Sunday's 19-17 loss to the Jaguars.
news.head: Dallas Goedert comes up with six catches in Week 5
news.impact: Playing for the first time since Week 2, Goedert led the Eagles in targets and receptions on Sunday. Top wide receiver DeVonta Smith (hamstring) missed a second consecutive game, so Goedert's volume was at least somewhat attributable to that. Still, the veteran TE has long been a trusted target for QB Jalen Hurts. Goedert is coming off career bests with 60 receptions and 11 touchdowns last season.

news.body: Dallas Goedert will return on Sunday against the Jaguars.
news.head: Dallas Goedert (knee) will play Sunday
news.impact: Goedert will be back from a multi-week absence. He should be a borderline TE1 with DeVonta Smith and Saquon Barkley both still ruled out.

news.body: Dallas Goedert was seen practicing again on Thursday.
news.head: Dallas Goedert (knee) practices Thursday
news.impact: Goedert opened the week with a limited practice. He could have a chance to return on Sunday if he can practice all week. If not, a return in Week 6 becomes likely.

news.body: Dallas Goedert (knee) was officially limited at practice on Wednesday.
news.head: Dallas Goedert (knee) officially limited Wednesday
news.impact: Goedert was able to take part in Wednesday's practice and was officially a limited participant. That's a good sign after he has missed several weeks with a knee issue, as it indicates that he may be back in the lineup very soon. That will be great news for QB Jalen Hurts when that happens, as he has struggled mightily without his veteran tight end.

news.body: Dalton Kincaid caught one of his two targets for a seven-yard gain and added a two-point conversion catch in a 37-34 overtime win over the Rams in Week 5.
news.head: Dalton Kincaid catches one pass in Week 5
news.impact: Kincaid was quiet on Monday night, his second straight slow outing. After starting the season hot, Kincaid has just two catches for 14 yards over his past two contests. Overall, the veteran tight end has 16 catches for 277 yards and one touchdown through five games. He will be a low-end TE1 in Week 6 against the Raiders.

news.body: Dalton Kincaid caught 1-of-2 targets for seven yards in the loss to the Patriots.
news.head: Dalton Kincaid quiet in Week 4
news.impact: Kincaid set new season lows in all receiving metrics in the loss Sunday. Fantasy managers will hope that Kincaid bounces back in a Week 5 matchup against the Rams.

news.body: Dalton Kincaid hauled in two of his three targets for 38 yards and one fumble lost in the Bills' 24-16 Week 3 win over the Los Angeles Chargers.
news.head: Dalton Kincaid quiet in Week 3 win over Chargers
news.impact: Kincaid was held in check by the Los Angeles defense, failing to surpass 90 receiving yards for the first time in three contests in the win. The tight end remains one of the more impactful pass-catching options for quarterback Josh Allen, with a Week 4 divisional matchup against the New England Patriots up next.

news.body: Dalton Kincaid caught 7-of-8 passing attempts for 95 yards and a touchdown in Thursday night's 41-31 win over the Detroit Lions.
news.head: Dalton Kincaid electric in win Thursday
news.impact: Kincaid's great start to the season continued on Thursday night. He was Buffalo's leading receiver against the Lions and was able to get into the end zone on one of his seven catches, which left him with a great fantasy total. It looks like he may be in the midst of a big breakout season right now, so long as he and QB Josh Allen stay healthy for the majority of the season.

news.body: Dalton Schultz caught 4-of-6 targets for 33 yards in the Texans' 34-31 win over the Jaguars.
news.head: Dalton Schultz hauls in four passes in Week 6
news.impact: Schultz's six targets are his most since a Week 2 performance that saw him log 12 receptions on 14 targets. Foster Moreau was targeted more in the end zone, resulting in two touchdowns Sunday. The veteran remains an emergency start at best for fantasy managers.

news.body: Dalton Schultz caught 3-of-4 targets for 30 yards in the Texans 26-3 win over the Titans.
news.head: Dalton Schultz catches three passes Sunday
news.impact: Schultz remains closer to the TE2 range for fantasy managers with Nico Collins healthy.

news.body: Dalton Schultz caught 2-of-2 targets for nine yards in the Texans 34-30 loss against the Cowboys.
news.head: Dalton Schultz quiet Sunday
news.impact: Schultz continues to be less reliable for fantasy managers with Nico Collins on the field.

news.body: Dalton Schultz caught all three of his targets for 30 yards in a 19-17 loss to the Colts.
news.head: Dalton Schultz hauls in three catches in Week 3
news.impact: Schultz saw his lowest target share of the season Sunday and had an incredible drop of from his 12 receptions in Week 2. The Houston offense struggled in general against the Colts' defense, and they will need to bounce back against Dallas to avoid going 0-4 on the season.

news.body: Darnell Washington caught 3-of-5 targets for 27 yards and a touchdown in Thursday's 27-24 loss to the Browns.
news.head: Darnell Washington hits paydirt in Week 4 loss
news.impact: Washington scored for the first time this season in Thursday's game. The towering TE has been productive in each of the last two games, hauling in six passes for 94 yards. He's still a risky fantasy option, with QB Aaron Rodgers spreading the ball around to a plethora of receivers.

news.body: Darnell Washington caught 3-of-4 targets for 67 yards in a 30-27 win over the Bengals.
news.head: Darnell Washington hauls in three passes in Week 3
news.impact: Washington saw the bulk of his production come on a 47-yard reception. The 25-year-old continues to compete with Pat Freiermuth for targets, with neither option being trustworthy heading into a Week 4 matchup with the Browns.

news.body: Darnell Washington (personal) is set to play in Sunday's game against the New England Patriots.
news.head: Darnell Washington (personal) set to play Sunday
news.impact: Washington missed two practices while tending to a personal issue earlier in the week, but he carries no designation heading into the weekend and will be available to play against the Patriots. He doesn't project to have fantasy relevance for the foreseeable future, however.

news.body: Darnell Washington (personal) returned to practice on Friday.
news.head: Darnell Washington (personal) back at practice Friday
news.impact: Washington missed Wednesday's and Thursday's practice session for personal reasons, but the big TE was back Friday. Washington secured both of his targets for 18 yards in Week 1's win over the Falcons.

news.body: Carolina Panthers tight end Darren Waller did not record a reception on two targets in a Week 6 win over Philadelphia.
news.head: Darren Waller blanked in Week 6
news.impact: Waller's two targets were his fewest since Week 1. He had 14 between Weeks 3 and 4 heading into a Week 5 bye, but tight end Tommy Tremble got involved with two touchdowns in Week 6. The Panthers' offense has been potent, but Tremble has been involved as well with 11 catches in the last three games.

news.body: Darren Waller (toe) was limited at practice again on Thursday.
news.head: Darren Waller (toe) limited again Thursday
news.impact: The veteran tight end was a limited participant for another practice on Thursday. His toe injury doesn't seem to be a serious issue, but there's always a chance that it will leave him out for a week. Tommy Tremble (rib) would see more work if that's the case.

news.body: Darren Waller (toe) was limited at practice on Wednesday.
news.head: Darren Waller (toe) limited at practice Wednesday
news.impact: Carolina left the veteran limited at practice on Wednesday. They are likely trying to limit his workload early on in the week, so fantasy managers shouldn't be too concerned with his availability for Week 6 at this point, unless he's downgraded at some point later on in the week.

news.body: Darren Waller hauled in 3-of-6 targets for 36 yards in Sunday's 32-26 win over the Lions.
news.head: Darren Waller catches three passes Sunday night
news.impact: In a game where Bryce Young cleared 300 yards passing and two of Carolina's top three wide receivers were out with injury, much more should have been expected from Waller. However, nearly half of Young's completions went to Tetairoa McMillan, who finished with almost 200 yards and a pair of touchdowns. That just did not leave much for Waller or any other Carolina route runner. The veteran remains a TD-dependent TE2.

news.body: Evan Engram caught both of his targets for 13 yards in the Broncos' 17-14 win over Seattle on Thursday.
news.head: Evan Engram catches two passes in win
news.impact: Engram had a nice grab in this game, but that was about it for his highlights. He should not be started in any format right now.

news.body: Evan Engram caught all four of his targets for 55 yards in Sunday's 23-17 win over the Chargers.
news.head: Evan Engram leads the Broncos in receiving Sunday
news.impact: Engram bounced back Sunday from a string of games in which he produced very little for the Broncos offense. The veteran tight end led the team in receptions and yards, going over the 50-yard mark for the first time this season. It's a positive step, but the Broncos passing game is still suspect and Engram remains a lower-end TE for fantasy purposes at the moment.

news.body: Evan Engram caught one of his five targets for six yards in Sunday's 24-14 loss to the San Francisco 49ers.
news.head: Evan Engram quiet in loss Sunday
news.impact: Engram had another disappointing performance despite seeing five targets. Turning those opportunities into just one catch for six yards isn't going to get it done for fantasy managers. The target volume at least gives him something to build on, but Engram will be difficult to trust in 12-team leagues or shallower until he starts producing more with his opportunities.

news.body: Evan Engram failed to catch either of his two targets in Sunday night's 30-26 win over the Los Angeles Rams.
news.head: Evan Engram silent in win Sunday
news.impact: Engram had another disappointing game on Sunday night, this time failing to finish with even a single catch against the Rams. He shouldn't be rostered in most league formats moving forward after two very poor performances back-to-back.

news.body: George Kittle caught 5-of-6 targets for 24 yards in the 49ers 32-29 win over the Seahawks.
news.head: George Kittle catches five passes Sunday
news.impact: Kittle was used as a dump off pass catcher from Brock Purdy all afternoon. He'll look to bounce back next week against the Commanders.

news.body: 49ers TE George Kittle (illness) is officially active for a Week 5 matchup with the Seahawks.
news.head: George Kittle (illness) officially active for Week 5
news.impact: It was announced that Kittle was dealing with an illness, but the star tight end will suit up and play Sunday. Kittle should slot in as a TE1 this week despite the illness.

news.body: George Kittle caught four of his six targets for 70 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 24-14 win over the Denver Broncos.
news.head: George Kittle scores long touchdown in win Sunday
news.impact: Most of Kittle's production came on one play, but fantasy managers won't complain. He took a short pass 56 yards for a touchdown late in the fourth quarter to put the game away. Kittle remains a middle-of-the-pack TE1 in fantasy when healthy.

news.body: George Kittle caught 6-of-7 targets for 82 yards and two touchdowns in the 49ers 36-30 win over the Cardinals on Sunday.
news.head: George Kittle scores twice Sunday
news.impact: Kittle took on a bigger role with Mike Evans (rib) exiting early. He hauled in two touchdowns from Brock Purdy in the win. He remains a strong TE1, especially if Evans misses time.

news.body: Cleveland Browns tight end Harold Fannin Jr. was limited to one reception for nine yards on three targets in Week 6.
news.head: Harold Fannin Jr. catches one pass in Week 6
news.impact: Fannin had his second consecutive week with just one catch after averaging 5.0 receptions and 1.0 touchdowns from Weeks 2-4. Deshaun Watson has been held to under 175 passing yards in three of the last four weeks, putting a lid on the team's aerial output.

news.body: Harold Fannin Jr. caught one of his four targets for four yards in a 17-12 loss to the Jets in Week 5.
news.head: Harold Fannin Jr. held to one catch in Week 5
news.impact: It was the first time in Fannin's 21-game NFL career that he was held to fewer than two catches, although a rainy afternoon at MetLife Stadium may have played into the slow outing. The second-year tight end now has 18 catches for 157 yards and three touchdowns through five games. He will look to bounce back at home in Week 6 against the Ravens.

news.body: Harold Fannin Jr. came up with 3-of-5 targets for 27 yards and a touchdown in Thursday's 27-24 win over the Steelers.
news.head: Harold Fannin Jr. finds the end zone again in Week 4
news.impact: After scoring twice in Week 3, Fannin hauled in another touchdown toss from Deshaun Watson on Thursday night. Fannin did not start off great in a season-opening loss to the Jaguars, but during the Browns' current three-game winning streak, the second-year pro has totaled 15 grabs for 132 yards. Fannin is cementing his TE1 status.

news.body: Harold Fannin Jr. hauled in 7-of-9 targets for 51 yards and two touchdowns in Sunday's 21-18 win over the Carolina Panthers.
news.head: Harold Fannin Jr. hauls in two touchdowns Sunday
news.impact: Fannin had a great game on Sunday. He was Cleveland's leader in receptions and yards against the Panthers, and he was also able to get into the end zone twice to put the cherry on top. Fantasy managers should be happy with his performance in this game but should expect struggles with consistency for him moving forward.

news.body: Hunter Henry caught 4-of-5 targets for 48 yards and a touchdown in a 26-19 win over the Jets.
news.head: Hunter Henry hits pay dirt in Week 6 win
news.impact: Henry has found the endzone in two consecutive games and logged at least four targets or more in four of his last five games. Henry remains a trustworthy option heading into a Week 7 matchup with the Bears.

news.body: Hunter Henry caught 3-of-4 targets for 44 yards and a touchdown in the Patriots win over the Raiders.
news.head: Hunter Henry hauls in three passes in Week 5
news.impact: Henry found the end zone on an 11-yard touchdown reception late in the second quarter. This marks Henry's first touchdown of the season and gives Henry back-to-back-games with four or more targets. Henry and the Patriots will take on the Jets in Week 6.

news.body: Hunter Henry caught all five of his targets for 62 yards in the Patriots win over the Bills.
news.head: Hunter Henry hauls in five passes in Week 4 win
news.impact: Henry led the team in receiving yards, and caught the pass to seal the win late in the fourth quarter. His five receptions and 62 yards mark new season highs for the veteran. Henry will look to build on this performance against the Raiders in Week 5.

news.body: Hunter Henry caught 1-of-2 targets for just five yards in Sunday's 35-6 loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars.
news.head: Hunter Henry a non-factor in loss Sunday
news.impact: The veteran tight end wasn't able to contribute for the Patriots on Sunday. He finished with just one five-yard catch against the Jaguars, which left him with a very poor fantasy total. He can't be trusted as a streaming option in most leagues moving forward.

news.body: Isaiah Likely caught 6-of-11 targets for 99 yards and a touchdown in the Giants 34-27 loss against the Saints.
news.head: Isaiah Likely hauls in touchdown Sunday
news.impact: Likely continued his success at finding the end zone. He nearly caught a second one as J.J. McCarthy just missed looking to find him to tie the game at the end of the game. He remains a locked in TE1.

news.body: Isaiah Likely is practicing in full for Week 6 against the Saints.
news.head: Isaiah Likely (foot) practicing in full for Week 6
news.impact: Likely remains a strong TE1 for fantasy managers.

news.body: Isaiah Likely hauled in 11 of his 13 targets for 94 yards and two touchdowns in the Giants' 27-27 tie with the Washington Commanders in Week 5.
news.head: Isaiah Likely hauls in two touchdowns in Week 5 tie with Commanders
news.impact: Likely has made the most of his involvement in the New York passing attack to this point, recording over 65 receiving yards in three of the first five games. The tight end remains one of the more impactful options in the Giants offense early on for new head coach John Harbaugh ahead of a Week 6 matchup against the New Orleans Saints.

news.body: Isaiah Likely is off the injury report for Sunday's game against the Commanders.
news.head: Isaiah Likely (knee/groin) off injury report Sunday
news.impact: Likely hauled in seven passes last week. He remains a borderline TE1/TE2 play for fantasy managers.

news.body: Jake Ferguson caught three of six targets for 19 yards in the Cowboys' 24-16 loss to Tampa Bay on Thursday.
news.head: Jake Ferguson has critical drop in loss to Bucs
news.impact: Ferguson had a critical drop on the Cowboys' final drive as they were trying to tie the game, failing to catch a pass and instead bobbling it straight up and into the arms of LB Alex Anzalone. It was a tough night for the veteran, but better days will come.

news.body: Jake Ferguson caught 3-of-4 targets for 11 yards in the Cowboys 34-30 win over the Texans.
news.head: Jake Ferguson quiet Sunday
news.impact: Ferguson spent most of the afternoon blocking against the Texans pass rush. He remains a touchdown dependent tight end on a week-to-week basis.

news.body: Jake Ferguson caught three of his five targets for 23 yards and a touchdown while losing a fumble in a 34-31 loss to the Ravens in Brazil in Week 3.
news.head: Jake Ferguson finds the end zone in Week 3
news.impact: Ferguson hauled in a 19-yard touchdown pass from Dak Prescott in the third quarter. The veteran tight end has racked up nine catches for 72 yards and three touchdowns through three games this season. He will be on the TE1 radar in Week 4's matchup against a tough Houston defense.

news.body: Jake Ferguson caught all four of his targets for 43 yards and two touchdowns in the Cowboys win over the Commanders.
news.head: Jake Ferguson finds the end zone twice in Week 2
news.impact: Ferguson was quiet in Week 1, so this was a much needed bounce back performance. The 27-year-old remains the primary pass catching option out of the tight end group. Ferguson will look to build on this performance in Week 3 against the Ravens.

news.body: Juwan Johnson did not catch either of his two targets in the Saints 34-27 win over the Giants.
news.head: Juwan Johnson does not haul in pass Sunday
news.impact: It was a low-volume passing day for New Orleans. Johnson will look to bounce back next week against the Steelers.

news.body: Juwan Johnson caught four of his five targets for 16 yards in the Saints' 23-13 loss to the Minnesota Vikings in Week 5.
news.head: Juwan Johnson quiet in Week 5 loss
news.impact: Johnson struggled to make an impact against a tough Minnesota defense, finishing with under 50 receiving yards for the first time in five contests. The tight end will look to get back on track against the New York Giants in Week 6.

news.body: Juwan Johnson hauled in 6-of-8 targets for 59 yards in Monday night's 45-24 loss to the Atlanta Falcons.
news.head: Juwan Johnson hauls in six passes Monday
news.impact: The veteran tight end had a nice outing on Monday night. He finished with six receptions for 59 yards over the course of the game, although he wasn't able to get into the end zone at all, which left him with a mediocre fantasy total. He will continue to be a reliable week-to-week option until Jordyn Tyson (hamstring) is available to make his debut for the Saints.

news.body: Juwan Johnson caught 8-of-8 targets for 53 yards in the Saints 35-27 loss against the Raiders on Sunday.
news.head: Juwan Johnson catches two touchdowns Sunday
news.impact: It must have been tight end day in New Orleans as the two teams combined for six touchdowns caught by tight ends. Johnson remains a steady weekly play for fantasy managers.

news.body: Kenyon Sadiq caught 1-of-3 targets for 12 yards in a 26-19 loss to the Patriots.
news.head: Kenyon Sadiq records one reception in Week 6
news.impact: Sadiq returned from a concussion that he suffered in Week 5, but was not a featured part of the offense. Mason Taylor saw six targets to Sadiq's three, so both appear to be involved in the offense heading into Week 7.

news.body: Jets TE Kenyon Sadiq (concussion) is officially active for a Week 6 matchup with the Patriots.
news.head: Kenyon Sadiq (concussion) officially active for Week 6
news.impact: Sadiq has cleared concussion protocol and will play against the Patriots after being listed questionable heading into Sunday. Sadiq and Mason Taylor will likely split time at tight end against New England.

news.body: Kenyon Sadiq (concussion) practices in full Friday.
news.head: Kenyon Sadiq (concussion) looks good to go for Week 6
news.impact: Sadiq looks to be finishing up his time in the league's concussion protocol on Friday. The rookie tight end is expected to play Sunday against the Patriots.

news.body: Kenyon Sadiq (concussion) was limited at practice again on Thursday.
news.head: Kenyon Sadiq (concussion) limited again Thursday
news.impact: The rookie is at risk of being sidelined on Sunday. He's still going through the NFL's concussion protocols and remained limited for another practice on Thursday as a result. If he's unable to play, look for Mason Taylor to again serve as New York's top tight end in his absence.

news.body: Kyle Pitts Sr. hauled in five of his seven targets for 60 yards and two touchdowns in the Falcons' 31-23 Week 6 loss to the Chicago Bears.
news.head: Kyle Pitts Sr. hauls in two touchdowns in Week 6 loss to Bears
news.impact: Pitts Sr. has made the most of the return of quarterback Michael Penix Jr., recording five receptions and one or more touchdowns in each of the last two contests. The tight end remains one of the primary pass-catching options for head coach Kevin Stefanski as long as Penix Jr. is behind center ahead of a Week 7 matchup against the San Francisco 49ers.

news.body: Kyle Pitts Sr. brought down 5-of-6 targets for 42 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 30-23 OT loss to the Ravens.
news.head: Kyle Pitts Sr. hauls in first touchdown of the season
news.impact: After being a non-factor over the first three weeks of the season, Pitts has asserted himself the last two games. Over the last two weeks, Pitts has caught eight passes for 89 yards and hit paydirt for the first time Sunday night. Unfortunately, QB Michael Penix's (ribs) health is once again in question, so Pitts is a real question mark at tight end for fantasy purposes.

news.body: Kyle Pitts Sr. caught three passes for 47 yards in Monday night's 45-24 win over the New Orleans Saints.
news.head: Kyle Pitts Sr. racks up 47 yards Monday
news.impact: Pitts has had a very rough start to the season from a fantasy perspective, and it didn't get much better on Monday. He was able to rack up 47 yards at least, but he only caught three passes and failed to get into the end zone at all. He shouldn't be trusted as a starter for the foreseeable future.

news.body: Kyle Pitts Sr. caught just one of two targets for five yards in the Falcons' 35-14 win over the Packers on Thursday.
news.head: Kyle Pitts Sr. snags single pass in win
news.impact: Pitts took a backseat to Drake London and Bijan Robinson in this game, with Michael Penix heavily favoring London in terms of target share. Pitts was productive last year both with London on and off the field, but Penix has been so fixated on London in his starts that it's tough to trust Pitts. He is a bit of a shaky fantasy start until his workload improves.

news.body: Baltimore Ravens tight end Mark Andrews caught just one pass for four yards in the Week 6 road loss against the Cleveland Browns
news.head: Mark Andrews quiet in Week 6 loss
news.impact: Andrews saw a season-low three targets in a tight contest with rookie tight end Josh Cuevas catching the lone touchdown of the night. The veteran has been held under 30 yards for four consecutive weeks while providing a low-end fantasy output.

news.body: Mark Andrews secured 4-of-6 targets for 28 yards in Sunday's 30-23 OT win against the Falcons.
news.head: Mark Andrews grabs four passes in Week 5 win
news.impact: Andrews limited PPR contribution was diminished by a lost fumble Sunday night. The veteran TE finished behind wide receivers Zay Flowers and Rashod Bateman in both catches and yards. Andrews is still a significant factor in the Ravens' offense, as he's caught 22 passes through five games. However, he's scored just once and is averaging barely over 8.0 yards per reception.

news.body: Mark Andrews caught 5-of-6 targets for 27 yards and a touchdown in the Ravens win over the Titans.
news.head: Mark Andrews finds the end zone in Week 4 win
news.impact: Andrews caught a three-yard touchdown pass late in the second quarter to extend the Ravens' lead. This marked the veteran's first trip to the end zone this season. Andrews will look to build on this performance against the Falcons in Week 5.

news.body: Mark Andrews caught three of his five targets for 24 yards in a 34-31 win over the Cowboys in Week 3.
news.head: Mark Andrews goes for 24 yards in Week 3 win
news.impact: Andrews left the game in Brazil briefly with a hand injury but was able to return to action. The veteran tight end finished third on the Ravens in receiving in the contest. Andrews has now caught 13 passes for 122 yards through three games. He will be a high-end TE2 heading into Week 4 against the Titans.

news.body: Michael Mayer caught his lone target for two yards in a loss to the Patriots.
news.head: Michael Mayer disappears in Week 5 loss
news.impact: Mayer's one target set a new season low for the 25-year-old tight end. With Brock Bowers continuing to dominate the target share, Mayer is tough to trust in Week 6 against Buffalo.

news.body: Michael Mayer caught eight of his 10 targets for 82 yards in a 30-27 loss to the Chiefs in Week 4.
news.head: Michael Mayer goes for 82 yards in Week 4
news.impact: Mayer finished second on the team in receiving behind only Brock Bowers. His involvement alongside Bowers has been encouraging as Mayer caught a touchdown back in Week 3. Mayer is worth a look as a tight end streamer in deeper fantasy leagues going forward. He will face the Patriots in Week 5.

news.body: Michael Mayer caught 3-of-3 targets for 32 yards and a touchdown in the Raiders 35-27 win over the Saints on Sunday.
news.head: Michael Mayer hauls in touchdown Sunday
news.impact: Mayer still made an impact despite the return of Brock Bowers. It was tight end day in New Orleans as the two teams combined for six touchdowns scored by tight ends.

news.body: Michael Mayer caught 3-of-4 targets for 23 yards in Sunday's 26-14 win over the Los Angeles Chargers.
news.head: Michael Mayer catches three passes Sunday
news.impact: Sunday's game brought less involvement for Mayer, as he had half of the receptions that he had in the season opener a week before. He was only able to rack up 23 yards over the course of the afternoon, and now he is set to once again be an irrelevant fantasy option with Brock Bowers (knee) soon to make his return to the lineup.

news.body: Noah Fant caught his only target for seven yards in the Saints' 23-13 loss to the Minnesota Vikings in Week 5.
news.head: Noah Fant catches one pass in Week 5
news.impact: Fant has struggled to make a consistent impact in the New Orleans passing attack, finishing with less than 35 receiving yards in each of his four contests. The tight end remains a risky pass-catching option in all formats ahead of a Week 6 contest against the New York Giants.

news.body: Noah Fant (abdomen) was a limited participant at practice on Thursday.
news.head: Noah Fant (abdomen) limited participant Thursday
news.impact: Fant was limited for another practice on Thursday as he continues to recover from an injury to his abdomen. He seems to be trending towards playing in Week 5, but we won't know his status for sure until after practice on Friday.

news.body: Noah Fant (abdomen) was limited at practice on Wednesday.
news.head: Noah Fant (abdomen) limited Wednesday
news.impact: The Saints were without Fant in Week 4, as he was sidelined due to the same abdomen issue that left him limited at practice on Wednesday. He seems to be trending towards playing in Week 5, but we won't get official word until later on in the week.

news.body: Noah Fant caught 4-of-4 targets for 33 yards and two touchdowns in the Saints 35-27 loss against the Raiders on Sunday.
news.head: Noah Fant hauls in two touchdowns Sunday
news.impact: Fant and Juwan Johnson both hauled in two touchdowns on the day. Despite that, Fant remains off the fantasy radar.

news.body: Oronde Gadsden II failed to catch his only target in Sunday's 23-17 loss to the Broncos.
news.head: Oronde Gadsden II targeted just once in Week 5 loss
news.impact: Even with the Chargers' receiving corps a bit beaten up, Gadsden was a non-factor for the offense. This came a week after catching a season-high five passes for 36 yards. Gadsden, as with the Chargers' offense on the whole, just cannot be depended on at present.

news.body: Oronde Gadsden II caught 5-of-8 targets for 36 yards in the Chargers 30-23 loss against the Seahawks.
news.head: Oronde Gadsden II catches five passes Sunday
news.impact: Gadsden was a safety blanket for Justin Herbert with his longest reception going for nine yards. He'll be a TE2 play next week against the Broncos.

news.body: Oronde Gadsden II failed to catch any of his three targets in the Chargers' 24-16 loss to the Buffalo Bills in Week 3.
news.head: Oronde Gadsden II sees three targets in Week 3
news.impact: Gadsden II has been minimally involved in the Los Angeles passing attack early on, seeing three targets or less in each of the first three games. The tight end remains difficult to trust ahead of a Week 4 contest against the Seattle Seahawks.

news.body: Chargers head coach Jim Harbaugh said TE Oronde Gadsden II is "ready to step up."
news.head: Oronde Gadsden II 'ready to step up' per HC Jim Harbaugh
news.impact: Gadsden will be stepping into a bigger role with both David Njoku and Charlie Kolar sidelined. He'll be a viable streamer for fantasy managers.

news.body: Steelers TE Pat Freiermuth (calf) is officially active for a Week 6 matchup with Tampa Bay.
news.head: Pat Freiermuth (calf) officially active for Week 6
news.impact: Freiermuth was a late addition to the injury report this week, but has been cleared to play after pregame warmups. The veteran has appeared more involved in the offense as of late, scoring three touchdowns in his last two games.

news.body: Pat Freiermuth has been added to the injury report as questionable for Sunday’s game against the Buccaneers.
news.head: Pat Freiermuth (calf) now questionable Sunday
news.impact: Freiermuth was a late addition to the injury report with a calf injury. His status will need to be monitored Sunday morning.

news.body: Pat Freiermuth caught five of seven targets for 44 yards and two scores in the Steelers' 34-22 win over the Colts on Sunday.
news.head: Pat Freiermuth hauls in two touchdowns in win
news.impact: Friermuth had a day against the Colts, especially in the red zone, where he caught two of Aaron Rodgers' three touchdowns. The Muth doesn't get heavy volume, but he's been a streamable option so far this year, and that seems like it will continue.

news.body: Pat Freiermuth caught 3-of-5 targets for 17 yards and a touchdown in Thursday's 27-24 loss to the Browns.
news.head: Pat Freiermuth catches touchdown in Week 4 loss
news.impact: Freiermuth scored for the second time this season and the first time since Week 1 during Thursday's loss. The veteran TE has gotten at least four targets in each of the Steelers' first four games, but he's averaging just over 31 yards per game. Freiermuth should be viewed as a TD-dependent streamer at present.

news.body: Sam LaPorta caught five passes for 88 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 45-21 win over the Arizona Cardinals.
news.head: Sam LaPorta stellar in win Sunday
news.impact: LaPorta looked great again on Sunday, finishing as Detroit's leading receiver with 88 yards and a touchdown on five catches against the Cardinals. He has been playing very well and remains a must-start fantasy option for the time being.

news.body: Sam LaPorta caught 8-of-13 targets for 84 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 32-26 loss to the Panthers.
news.head: Sam LaPorta hits paydirt in Sunday's loss
news.impact: LaPorta put up new season highs in receptions and yards Sunday night, tying for the team lead with eight grabs. LaPorta also scored for the second time this season. He's not a sure thing every week, but LaPorta is a definite top-10 TE with top-five upside the rest of the way.

news.body: Sam LaPorta caught 3-of-4 targets for 44 yards in a 31-24 win over the Jets.
news.head: Sam LaPorta tallies three receptions in Week 3
news.impact: LaPorta saw the bulk of the targets go to Amon-Ra St. Brown and Jahmyr Gibbs in the win over the Jets. Fantasy managers will hope that LaPorta can become more involved against the Panthers in Week 4.

news.body: Sam LaPorta hauled in 6-of-7 targets for 52 yards and a touchdown in Thursday night's 41-31 loss to the Buffalo Bills.
news.head: Sam LaPorta hauls in touchdown Thursday
news.impact: LaPorta had a good showing on Thursday night. He caught all but one of his targets and turned that into 52 yards and a touchdown in a shootout loss against the Buffalo Bills. He might struggle with consistency moving forward but will continue to have as high of a TD upside as anyone for the foreseeable future.

news.body: Travis Kelce caught four passes for 53 yards in the Chiefs' 22-6 win over the Chargers in Week 6.
news.head: Travis Kelce Records 53 Receiving Yards in Week 6
news.impact: Kelce wasn't needed for a big performance with Kansas City controlling the game behind Walker and its defense. Still, 53 yards kept his floor intact despite failing to score. Kelce remains a weekly low-end TE1.

news.body: Travis Kelce caught two of his four targets for 15 yards in a 30-27 win over the Raiders in Week 4.
news.head: Travis Kelce quiet in Week 4 win
news.impact: Kelce was quiet in the win as Tyquan Thornton and Xavier Worthy did most of the damage in the passing attack. Kelce has been a solid fantasy tight end this season, catching 16 passes for 246 yards and two touchdowns in four games. He will be on bye in Week 5 before taking on the Chargers in Week 6.

news.body: Travis Kelce hauled in both of his targets for 59 yards and one touchdown in the Chiefs' 24-10 Week 3 win over the Miami Dolphins.
news.head: Travis Kelce finds end zone in Week 3 win over Dolphins
news.impact: Kelce has been impactful to begin the season, recording over 55 receiving yards in each of the first three contests. The veteran tight end has turned back the clock as part of a revamped Chiefs offense for head coach Andy Reid, with a Week 4 matchup against the Las Vegas Raiders up next.

news.body: Travis Kelce hauled in 9-of-11 targets for 101 yards and a touchdown in Sunday night's 33-30 overtime win over the Indianapolis Colts.
news.head: Travis Kelce dominant in overtime win Sunday
news.impact: Kelce looked great on Sunday night. He led the team in receptions and racked up 101 receiving yards on the night, a number which he failed to hit at all last season. His touchdown was the cherry on top for fantasy managers, and he will likely continue to have good week-to-week value if Patrick Mahomes and KC's offense continues to look this good moving forward.

news.body: Trey McBride hauled in 9-of-10 targets for 66 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 45-21 loss to the Detroit Lions.
news.head: Trey McBride hauls in touchdown Sunday
news.impact: The star tight end played well on Sunday. He was able to record 66 yards and a touchdown on his nine catches, which left him with a great fantasy total on the afternoon. He should continue to be great moving forward, even with Arizona not expected to win many games over the course of the season.

news.body: Trey McBride hauled in 7-of-12 targets for 31 yards in Sunday's 36-24 loss to the New York Giants.
news.head: Trey McBride hauls in seven passes Sunday
news.impact: McBride saw plenty of opportunities on Sunday, but he wasn't able to do much with them. His seven passes turned into just 31 yards, so if someone started him in a non-PPR league format, his fantasy finish was quite disappointing for them. He should bounce back and return to form sometime within the next week or two, however.

news.body: Trey McBride caught 9-of-11 targets for 75 yards in the Cardinals 36-30 loss against the Cardinals on Sunday.
news.head: Trey McBride hauls in nine passes Sunday
news.impact: McBride continues to be the safety blanket for Jacoby Brissett all over the field every week. He and Brock Bowers remain 1A and 1B among the tight end position.

news.body: Trey McBride caught eight of 10 targets for 41 yards and a score in the Cardinals' 31-7 loss to the Seahawks on Sunday.
news.head: Trey McBride snags touchdown in loss to Seattle
news.impact: McBride was the only thing working for the offense on Sunday, and even that only lasted but for so long. Seattle completely shut down the Cardinals in the second half, and McBride with them. But, it's doubtful any fantasy manager will complain about eight catches for 40+ yards and a score from their tight end.

news.body: Tucker Kraft caught all five of his targets for 64 yards while also rushing once for two yards in the Packers' 31-7 win over the Chicago Bears in Week 5.
news.head: Tucker Kraft sees six touches in Week 5
news.impact: Kraft has seen increased involvement in the Green Bay passing attack of late, logging five or more targets in each of his last three contests. The tight end will look to offer more impactful output moving forward, with a Week 6 contest against the Dallas Cowboys up next.

news.body: Tucker Kraft caught six of his seven targets for 42 yards and a touchdown while adding a three-yard run in a 17-14 win over the Buccaneers in Week 4.
news.head: Tucker Kraft finds the end zone in Week 4
news.impact: Kraft scored his first touchdown of the season on a two-yard pass from Jordan Love. The veteran tight end set a season-high in receptions in the game as he continues to ramp up after last season's ACL tear. Overall, Kraft has 15 catches for 148 yards and one touchdown. He will be a TE1 in fantasy in Week 5 against the Bears.

news.body: Tucker Kraft caught four of eight targets for 26 yards in the Packers' 35-14 loss to Atlanta on Thursday.
news.head: Tucker Kraft snags four passes in loss to Atlanta
news.impact: Kraft could have had a slightly bigger day had he held onto the football in what ended up being ruled a drop. The defensive back made a fantastic punch at the ball right as Kraft was corralling it into his chest, forcing a dropped pass. Kraft is still worth starting, and with that eight-target total, he has now beaten his season high in targets (previously six). The volume is there; the results just haven't quite followed yet.

news.body: Tucker Kraft caught two of his three targets for 15 yards in the Packers' 20-17 Week 2 win over the New York Jets.
news.head: Tucker Kraft quiet in Week 2 win
news.impact: Kraft was unable to make a significant impact as part of an underwhelming Green Bay passing attack, finishing with less than four receptions in each of the first two games. The tight end will look to get back on track for fantasy managers against the Atlanta Falcons in Week 3.

news.body: Tyler Higbee is off the injury report for Sunday's game against the Cardinals.
news.head: Tyler Higbee off injury report Sunday
news.impact: Higbee will be good to go despite not practicing on Friday.

news.body: Tyler Higbee caught five of his six targets for 83 yards in a 37-34 overtime loss to the Bills in Week 5.
news.head: Tyler Higbee goes for 83 yards in Week 5
news.impact: Higbee finished second on the Rams in receiving on Monday night, behind only Puka Nacua. The veteran tight end has earned a larger role in the team's offense thanks to some injuries in the LA tight-end room, having caught 18 passes for 212 yards and a touchdown over his past three contests. Higbee is looking like a solid fantasy option heading into Week 6 vs. Arizona.

news.body: Tyler Higbee is off the injury report for Monday's game against the Bills.
news.head: Tyler Higbee off injury report Monday
news.impact: Despite not practicing on Saturday, Higbee will be good to go in his usual role on Monday.

news.body: Tyler Higbee hauled in 5-of-6 targets for 67 yards in Sunday's 24-20 win over the Philadelphia Eagles.
news.head: Tyler Higbee solid in win Sunday
news.impact: The veteran tight end stepped up and played a bigger role again in Week 4. He did well with his opportunities, finishing with five catches for 67 yards in a win over the Eagles. He should continue to be a viable fantasy option with Terrance Ferguson (ankle) set to be sidelined for a few more weeks at least.

news.body: Colts TE Tyler Warren (groin) is officially inactive for Week 6.
news.head: Tyler Warren (groin) officially inactive for Week 6
news.impact: Warren was a late addition to the injury report this week and was only able to practice in a limited capacity Friday. Mo Alie-Cox will see the bulk of the playing time at tight end against the Titans.

news.body: Tyler Warren (groin) is now questionable for Sunday's game against the Tennessee Titans.
news.head: Tyler Warren (groin) now questionable for Sunday
news.impact: Warren is a surprise addition to Indianapolis' injury report. He seems to have aggravated his groin late in the practice week and was limited on Friday, and it may very well leave him sidelined in Week 6. Fantasy managers should keep close tabs on updates about his health over the next couple of days and should have a backup option ready in case the young tight end is ruled out.

news.body: Tyler Warren caught seven of nine targets for 83 yards and ran once for a one-yard score in the Colts' 34-22 loss to Pittsburgh.
news.head: Tyler Warren snags seven passes in loss
news.impact: Warren was one of the few bright spots for the Colts offense on a day when the offense stalled often, getting the team's only touchdown on a rush, and nearly doubling the yardage total of the second-highest receiver. The Colts have lacked explosiveness with Alec Pierce out, and that has caused all to suffer, including Warren. However, he's still getting it done thanks to volume, and should be a fine play most weeks.

news.body: Tyler Warren caught 5-of-5 targets for 41 yards in the Colts' 30-13 win over the Commanders.
news.head: Tyler Warren hauls in five passes in Week 4 win
news.impact: Warren and the rest of the Colts' pass catchers had a relatively quiet day as the team focused on the ground game. His five targets tie a season low, and Warren will look to become more involved in Week 5 against the Steelers.

news.body: Adonai Mitchell (finger) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Patriots.
news.head: Adonai Mitchell (finger) out for Week 6
news.impact: Mitchell will miss his fourth consecutive game this week. Rookie first-rounder Omar Cooper Jr. (ankle), veteran Tim Patrick, and Isaiah Williams should slot in behind Garrett Wilson in the WR pecking order for the Jets on Sunday.

news.body: Adonai Mitchell (finger) did not take part in New York's practice on Thursday.
news.head: Adonai Mitchell (finger) doesn't practice Thursday
news.impact: Mitchell was again a non-participant at practice on Thursday as he continues to recover from a finger injury. He will almost certainly be sidelined again in Week 6, but the potential return of rookie Omar Cooper Jr. (ankle) could help to offset the effects of Mitchell's likely absence.

news.body: Adonai Mitchell (finger) missed New York's practice on Wednesday.
news.head: Adonai Mitchell (finger) misses practice Wednesday
news.impact: Mitchell wasn't able to practice on Wednesday. He has missed some time while recovering from a finger injury, and it looks like he's trending towards missing another game in Week 6. We won't know his official status until later on in the week, however.

news.body: Jets coach Aaron Glenn said Adonai Mitchell remains week-to-week.
news.head: Adonai Mitchell (finger) still week-to-week
news.impact: Mitchell did have a surgical procedure to repair his injured finger. He will miss a fourth straight game.

news.body: A.J. Brown caught 3-of-10 targets for 27 yards in the Patriots' 26-19 win over the Jets.
news.head: A.J. Brown hauls in three passes in Week 6 win
news.impact: Brown struggled with drops Sunday, logging three drops in his return to action after a Week 1 ankle injury. Brown and the Patriots play on Thursday, so it is a quick turnaround for the veteran to knock off any additional rust heading into Week 7.

news.body: The Patriots activated A.J. Brown from injured reserve.
news.head: A.J. Brown (ankle) activated from IR
news.impact: Brown will make his return for the first time since Week 1. He'll be a WR2 with some risk in his first game back for fantasy managers.

news.body: A.J. Brown (ankle) is expected to be activated from IR on Saturday and play on Sunday against the Jets.
news.head: A.J. Brown (ankle) likely to be activated from IR on Saturday
news.impact: After a four game stint on IR with an ankle sprain, it looks like Brown will return. The Patriots receiver room has been a revolving door of production, with Romeo Doubs, Kyle Williams, and Efton Chism all seeing some sort of success with AJB out. Browns return will likely put Williams and Chism back in limited roles, but Doubs should still she the field fairly consistently.

news.body: A.J. Brown (ankle) is questionable to play in Sunday's game against the New York Jets.
news.head: A.J. Brown (ankle) questionable to play Sunday
news.impact: Brown was able to make his return to practice in a limited fashion this week, and he now carries a questionable tag heading into the weekend. Fantasy managers should pay close attention to all updates about his health over the next couple of days, as he will be an obvious player to start if active without restrictions, but that will be complicated if he is on a snap count or sidelined altogether this week.

news.body: Amon-Ra St. Brown caught 6-of-11 targets for 69 yards in Sunday's 45-21 win over the Arizona Cardinals.
news.head: Amon-Ra St. Brown racks up 69 yards Sunday
news.impact: The star wideout had an okay game on Sunday. He racked up 69 yards in an easy win over the Cardinals, but he wasn't able to get into the end zone at all, which left him with a mediocre fantasy total to his standards. He has had a great start to the season overall and should continue to be a high-end fantasy option moving forward.

news.body: Amon Ra St. Brown came up with 8-of-11 targets for 75 yards in Sunday's 32-26 loss to the Panthers.
news.head: Amon-Ra St. Brown makes eight grabs in Week 4 loss
news.impact: St. Brown failed to make it four straight games with a touchdown to start the season, but he still produced a solid showing. St. Brown has largely delivered for fantasy managers over the first quarter of the season, averaging nearly eight receptions for more than 75 yards with five scores to this point. He remains a certain WR1.

news.body: Amon-Ra St. Brown caught 4-of-8 targets for 19 yards and a touchdown in a 31-24 win over the Jets.
news.head: Amon-Ra St. Brown finds the end zone in Week 3 win
news.impact: St. Brown was not able to capitalize on his eight targets, but was able to help salvage the day with a touchdown in the second quarter. St. Brown now has five touchdowns through the first three games of the season and will look to build on a strong start to the season against the Panthers in Week 4.

news.body: Amon-Ra St. Brown caught 6-of-8 targets for 142 yards and two touchdowns in Thursday night's 41-31 loss to the Buffalo Bills.
news.head: Amon-Ra St. Brown scores twice in loss Thursday
news.impact: St. Brown was on fire on Thursday night. He had a slow start, but he ended up finishing the game with a team high in receptions and receiving yards while finding the end zone twice against the Bills. He will continue to be a top-tier fantasy option moving forward, especially in PPR scoring formats.

news.body: Antonio Williams caught all three of his targets for 31 yards in the Commanders' 27-27 tie with the New York Giants in Week 5.
news.head: Antonio Williams quiet in Week 5 tie
news.impact: Williams has struggled to make an impact of late, finishing with less than 35 receiving yards in each of the last four games.
