The wideout remains another risky pass-catching option in the Washington offense for head coach Dan Quinn, with a Week 6 contest against the San Francisco 49ers up next.

news.body: Antonio Williams caught 3-of-8 targets for 21 yards in the Commanders loss to the Colts.
news.head: Antonio Williams hauls in three passes in Week 4
news.impact: Williams was second on the team in targets, just one behind Stefon Diggs. Williams could continue to see more playing time next week if Terry McLaurin does not return from his hamstring injury.

news.body: Antonio Williams caught two of his four targets for 15 yards in the Commanders’ 33-31 Week 3 win over the Seattle Seahawks.
news.head: Antonio Williams quiet in Week 3 win
news.impact: Williams has fallen back to earth after an impressive showing in Week 1, finishing with less than 25 receiving yards in each of the last two games. The wideout remains a risky-pass catching option in an inconsistent offense early on, with a Week 4 matchup against the Indianapolis Colts up next.

news.body: Antonio Williams caught all three of his targets for 24 yards in the Commanders loss to the Cowboys.
news.head: Antonio Williams hauls in three passes in Week 2
news.impact: Williams saw his production dip from a strong Week 1 performance. The rookie wide receiver figures to lose some fantasy value with Jayden Daniels sidelined with an elbow injury. Williams and the Commanders will take on the Seahawks in Week 3.

news.body: Brandin Cooks hauled in a seven-yard touchdown on Sunday against the Seahawks.
news.head: Brandin Cooks catches touchdown Sunday
news.impact: Cooks took advantage of the opportunity with 49ers wide receivers going down with injuries. He could see some more opportunity heading into Week 6 against the Commanders, but he remains off the fantasy radar for now.

news.body: The 49ers signed WR Brandin Cooks to their practice squad.
news.head: Brandin Cooks signs with 49ers practice squad
news.impact: Cooks will be entering year 13 in the NFL. He'll add depth in the wide receiver room for San Francisco.

news.body: Brandin Cooks worked out with the Ravens on Thursday.
news.head: Brandin Cooks works out with Ravens
news.impact: The Ravens brought in the 32-year old for an official workout on Thursday. This comes in light of the fact that they may be without their top wideout for a short period of time, with Zay Flowers (hamstring) likely to be sidelined for a week or two at least. The workout ended without a deal for Cooks, but we could possibly see him join the team sometime within the next few weeks if they continue to need help at the wide receiver position.

news.body: Brandin Cooks delivered his best performance as a Bill during Sunday's 13-12 loss to Philadelphia, catching four of six targets for 101 yards. After managing just one catch over his first four games with the team, the veteran wideout stepped up in the absence of Dalton Kincaid (knee) and Keon Coleman (healthy scratch) to record his first 100-yard receiving game since 2021.
news.head: Brandin Cooks breaks out with 101 yards in loss
news.impact: Cooks finished second on the team in targets and receptions behind Khalil Shakir. This breakout effort could earn him a larger role as Buffalo gears up for the postseason. He will look to build on this momentum in the regular-season finale against the Jets in Week 18.

news.body: Brian Thomas Jr. was held without a catch on two targets in the Jaguars' 34-31 loss to the Texans.
news.head: Brian Thomas Jr. vanishes in Week 6 loss
news.impact: Thomas has now been held without a catch in two consecutive games, and did not see an offensive snap after halftime. Fantasy managers should feel comfortable benching Thomas, or at least moving on when the Jaguars return after their Week 7 bye.

news.body: Brian Thomas Jr. did not record a reception on three targets in Sunday's 19-17 win over the Eagles.
news.head: Brian Thomas Jr. puts up a goose egg in Week 5
news.impact: It is noteworthy that Thomas came up just a sideline toe touch short of scoring for the second straight week in this game. Still, Thomas has seen only six combined targets over the last three contests, and he seems to be in just a complementary role for the Jaguars at the moment.

news.body: Brian Thomas Jr. caught two passes for 17 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 22-17 win over the Cincinnati Bengals.
news.head: Brian Thomas Jr. finds end zone Sunday
news.impact: Thomas was able to haul in Jacksonville's lone passing touchdown against the Bengals. He wasn't able to do much outside of that, however, totaling just 17 yards over the course of the afternoon. He has had a slow start to the season and should not be considered a viable fantasy option for the foreseeable future.

news.body: Brian Thomas Jr. caught one pass for eight yards in Sunday's 35-6 blowout win over the New England Patriots.
news.head: Brian Thomas Jr. quiet in blowout win Sunday
news.impact: Thomas was a complete non-factor on Sunday. He caught just one pass over the course of the afternoon, and he was only able to turn that into eight yards on a day that Jacksonville's offense had no trouble scoring and moving the ball. He still has some potential given his talent, but he hasn't been productive for a while and shouldn't be started for the foreseeable future.

news.body: Dolphins WR Caleb Douglas (ankle) is officially inactive for a Week 5 matchup with the Bengals.
news.head: Caleb Douglas (ankle) officially inactive for Week 5
news.impact: Douglas was considered a long shot to play Sunday as he continues to recover from an ankle injury. Jalen Tolbert will likely see an increase in playing time with Douglas sidelined.

news.body: Dolphins WR Caleb Douglas is considered "unlikely" for Sunday's game against the Bengals.
news.head: Caleb Douglas (ankle) 'unlikely' to play in Week 5
news.impact: Douglas is expected to practice in some capacity on Friday. It won't be enough for him to play on Sunday, but he'll have a chance to return in Week 6.

news.body: Caleb Douglas (ankle) was officially a non-participant at practice on Thursday.
news.head: Caleb Douglas (ankle) officially a non-participant Thursday
news.impact: The rookie wasn't able to take part in Miami's practice on Thursday. He did some drills off to the side, but he still isn't healthy enough to make his return to practice. He isn't likely to play in Week 5, which will once again leave Malik Washington and Chris Bell (knee) with more work against the Bengals.

news.body: Caleb Douglas was seen working off to the side during practice on Thursday.
news.head: Caleb Douglas (ankle) working to side during practice Thursday
news.impact: Douglas did not practice on Wednesday and appears to be trending that way again on Thursday. He'll need to be monitored in practice on Friday.

news.body: Carnell Tate caught six of seven targets for 70 yards and a touchdown in the Titans' 26-20 win over the Colts on Sunday.
news.head: Carnell Tate snags touchdown in win over Colts
news.impact: Titans QB Cam Ward threw for 11 completions and 107 yards in this contest, meaning Tate accounted for over 50% of his completions and 65% of his passing yards. Only four Titans caught a pass on Sunday, and only Tate and Wan'Dale Robinson went over 10 yards. Tate has been a volume magnet so far this year, and it looks like he will continue to be. He's closing in on WR2 territory, but Ward's inconsistency will keep his floor low.

news.body: Carnell Tate caught 1-of-5 targets for six yards in the Titans 26-3 loss on Sunday against the Texans.
news.head: Carnell Tate quiet Sunday
news.impact: After a couple big performances, Tate was no where to be found this week. He'll be a WR3 play next week against the Colts.

news.body: Titans WR Carnell Tate (back) is officially active for a Week 5 matchup with Houston.
news.head: Carnell Tate (back) officially active for Week 5
news.impact: Tate was considered questionable after being limited in practice Thursday and Friday. He will suit up and provide the Titans with their best option at wide receiver against Houston.

news.body: Carnell Tate is listed as questionable for Sunday’s game against the Texans.
news.head: Carnell Tate (back) listed questionable Sunday
news.impact: Tate was limited in practice on Thursday and Friday. He should be on the favorable side of questionable heading into the weekend.

news.body: CeeDee Lamb is practicing in full for Week 6 against the Packers.
news.head: CeeDee Lamb (quad) practicing in full for Week 6
news.impact: Lamb left the game late last week with a quad injury. He remains a locked and loaded WR1.

news.body: CeeDee Lamb injured his quad during Thursday night's loss to the Buccaneers.
news.head: CeeDee Lamb sustains quad injury Thursday night
news.impact: Lamb finished Thursday's game with only two receptions on five targets for a total of nine yards. He bounced in and out of the contest after sustaining a quad injury, but he was clearly in pain and simply could not do much for the Cowboys' offense. On a positive note, the injury is considered to be mild, and the extra rest following a Thursday game should give Lamb time to recuperate.

news.body: CeeDee Lamb is off the injury report for Thursday’s game against the Buccaneers.
news.head: CeeDee Lamb (thigh) off injury report Thursday
news.impact: Lamb practiced in full all week. He remains a locked and loaded WR1.

news.body: CeeDee Lamb was a full participant in practice on Tuesday.
news.head: CeeDee Lamb (thigh) practices in full Tuesday
news.impact: Lamb remains a locked and loaded WR1 for Thursday’s game against the Buccaneers.

news.body: Chris Godwin Jr. caught all three of his targets for 37 yards in the Bucs' 24-16 win over the Cowboys on Thursday. He also ran once for three yards.
news.head: Chris Godwin Jr. snags three passes in win
news.impact: Godwin started off hot with two catches on the first drive, but fizzled out quickly with only a single catch the rest of the way. Emeka Egbuka was the favorite target of rookie QB Jaylon Daniels, with Godwin sitting tied for third on the team in targets behind Cade Otton and Kenny Gainwell. Godwin is a risky start at this point, and his value is more closely tied to real life than to fantasy.

news.body: Chris Godwin Jr. caught six of his seven targets for 31 yards in a 17-14 loss to the Packers in Week 4.
news.head: Chris Godwin Jr. hauls in six catches in Week 4
news.impact: Godwin led the Bucs in targets and catches but managed just 5.2 yards per catch in rookie quarterback Jalon Daniels' debut. The veteran wideout has 16 catches for 142 scoreless yards through four games this year. He will be a low-end flex option in Week 5 against Dallas.

news.body: Chris Godwin Jr. (ankle) is off of the injury report for Sunday's game against the Green Bay Packers.
news.head: Chris Godwin Jr. (ankle) off injury report for Sunday
news.impact: Godwin will be available to play on Sunday after logging a full practice on both Thursday and Friday. He shouldn't have any limitations but still doesn't project to be a good fantasy option against the Packers, especially with rookie Jalon Daniels starting at quarterback for the Buccaneers.

news.body: Chris Godwin Jr. (ankle) logged a full practice session on Thursday.
news.head: Chris Godwin Jr. (ankle) logs full practice Thursday
news.impact: The veteran was back at practice and participated in a full capacity on Thursday, meaning that he will almost certainly be a full go in Week 4. His absence on Wednesday was likely a load management move on the part of the team.

news.body: Chris Olave caught 4-of-7 targets for 43 yards and a touchdown in the Saints 34-27 win over the Giants.
news.head: Chris Olave hauls in touchdown Sunday
news.impact: It wasn't a huge day for Olave, but he made up for it with a touchdown. He will remain a WR1 heading into next week against the Steelers.

news.body: Saints WR Chris Olave (illness) is officially active for a Week 6 matchup with the Giants.
news.head: Chris Olave (illness) officially active for Week 6
news.impact: Olave was able to practice Friday but was listed as questionable to play as a precaution. The Saints will have their top pass catcher active against the Giants.

news.body: Chris Olave is listed as questionable for Sunday’s game against the Giants.
news.head: Chris Olave (illness) listed questionable Sunday
news.impact: Olave returned to practice on Friday. He should be on the favorable side of questionable heading into Sunday.

news.body: Chris Olave was back practicing on Friday.
news.head: Chris Olave (illness) returns to practice Friday
news.impact: Olave missed practice to start the week due to an illness. He should be good to go for Sunday's game against the Giants.

news.body: Christian Watson hauled in six of his team-leading eight targets for a team-high 143 yards and two touchdowns in the Packers' 31-7 Week 5 win over the Chicago Bears.
news.head: Christian Watson hauls in two touchdowns in Week 5 win over Bears
news.impact: Watson has had a nose for the end zone to begin the season, hauling in one or more touchdowns in four of the first five games. The wideout remains a dynamic pass-catching option in a Green Bay passing attack looking for more consistent output, with a Week 6 contest against the Dallas Cowboys up next.

news.body: Christian Watson caught all three of his targets for 47 yards in a 17-14 win over the Buccaneers in Week 4.
news.head: Christian Watson goes for 47 yards in Week 4
news.impact: Watson turned in his quietest game of the season but he still wound up leading the Packers in receiving yards. It was the first game all season where Watson failed to find the end zone, snapping a three-game scoring streak. Overall, Watson has 20 catches for 331 yards and four touchdowns through four games. He will be a WR1 in fantasy heading into Week 5 against the Bears.

news.body: Christian Watson carries no injury designation and will be good to go for Week 4's matchup against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.
news.head: Christian Watson good to go for Week 4
news.impact: There was some public concern when Watson seemed to favor one of his legs towards the end of last Thursday's game, but he is not listed on Green Bay's injury report for Week 4 and should be a full go against the Buccaneers. He remains a must-start fantasy option as often as he is healthy and on the field moving forward.

news.body: Christian Watson caught 7 of 10 targets for 96 yards and a touchdown in the Packers' 35-14 loss to the Falcons on Thursday.
news.head: Christian Watson extends touchdown streak to three games
news.impact: It might not have been in a win, but fantasy managers won't care. Watson has been a clear favorite target for Jordan Love, especially down in the red zone, with Tucker Kraft still working his way back to full health. He should be in your lineup whenever he is playing.

news.body: Cody White caught 2-of-4 targets for 44 yards in the Raiders loss to the Patriots.
news.head: Cody White hauls in two passes in Week 5
news.impact: White tied his season high in targets with four and set a new season high in receiving yardage. Fantasy managers can leave White off their radar for now.

news.body: Cody White (ankle) was a limited participant at practice on Wednesday.
news.head: Cody White (ankle) limited participant Wednesday
news.impact: White was able to practice in a limited fashion on Wednesday, though he's still being bothered by an ankle issue. It looks likely that he will play through it in Week 5, but we won't know for sure until later in the week.

news.body: The Raiders signed WR Cody White to their active roster.
news.head: Cody White signs with Raiders' active roster
news.impact: White has scored three touchdowns in the past two weeks. He gets the opportunity with Jack Bech (forearm) placed on IR.

news.body: Cody White caught 1-of-3 targets for four yards and a touchdown in the Raiders 35-27 win over the Saints on Sunday.
news.head: Cody White catches touchdown Sunday
news.impact: White now has three touchdowns in the past two weeks coming off the practice squad. Still be remains off the fantasy radar.

news.body: Cooper Kupp caught five of ten targets for 50 yards in the Seahawks' 17-14 loss to the Broncos on Thursday.
news.head: Cooper Kupp goes for 50 yards in loss
news.impact: Kupp had arguably his best game of the season, with season-highs in targets, receptions, and yards, lacking only a touchdown. He is a bit of a risky start most weeks, as his volume has been low for the most part. A near 20% target share this week is a nice sign of life, but we will need to see more consistency to really feel comfortable starting him.

news.body: Cooper Kupp caught 2-of-3 targets for 15 yards in the Seahawks 32-29 loss against the 49ers on Sunday.
news.head: Cooper Kupp part of crazy ending Sunday
news.impact: On 4th-and-10 with the game on the line, Kupp caught an 8-yard pass, made one defender miss and dove for the first down. After review, he wound up being short by one yard. He remains off the fantasy radar.

news.body: Cooper Kupp caught 1-of-2 targets for 13 yards in the Seahawks 30-23 win over the Chargers.
news.head: Cooper Kupp quiet Sunday
news.impact: Kupp remains off the fantasy radar in his current role.

news.body: Cooper Kupp caught four of his five targets for 46 yards and one touchdown in the Seahawks' 33-31 Week 3 loss to the Washington Commanders.
news.head: Cooper Kupp finds end zone in Week 3 loss
news.impact: Kupp took advantage of increased involvement in the Seattle passing attack, recording more than two receptions for the first time in three contests Sunday. The wideout remains difficult to trust in all formats ahead of a Week 4 contest against the Los Angeles Chargers.

news.body: Courtland Sutton caught two of three targets for 19 yards in the Broncos' 17-14 win over the Seahawks on Thursday.
news.head: Courtland Sutton catches two passes in win
news.impact: Sutton was quiet in this game, though there wasn't much to go around when the team combined for 107 passing yards. It's been a rough start to the year for QB Bo Nix, and until he improves, the pass catchers will suffer.

news.body: Courtland Sutton caught 2-of-3 targets for 18 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 23-17 win over the Chargers.
news.head: Courtland Sutton catches first touchdown of the season
news.impact: Sutton found the end zone for the first time this season during Sunday's win, but the veteran receiver still hasn't really gotten going. Sutton has finished with three or fewer receptions in all five weeks so far. He's also topped out at 46 yards. Sutton cannot be relied upon for much fantasy production in the Broncos' lackluster passing attack right now.

news.body: Courtland Sutton caught one of his six targets for four yards in Sunday's 24-14 loss to the San Francisco 49ers.
news.head: Courtland Sutton held to four yards Sunday
news.impact: Sutton had a rough day despite tying for the team lead among wide receivers with six targets. He and Bo Nix couldn't connect on several opportunities, leaving Sutton with just one catch. The volume remains encouraging, and fantasy managers shouldn't overreact to one bad game, but Sutton will need to bounce back first after his quiet Week 4 before entering starting lineups.

news.body: Courtland Sutton caught 3-of-7 targets for 46 yards in Sunday's 30-26 win over the Los Angeles Rams.
news.head: Courtland Sutton leads team in receiving Sunday
news.impact: Sutton was only able to haul in three out of his seven targets on Sunday night, but that was enough for him to rack up a team-high 46 yards on the night. Still, he hasn't been a good fantasy option so far this season and doesn't project to get much better anytime soon.

news.body: Cyrus Allen didn't see a target or touch in Sunday night's 33-30 overtime win over the Indianapolis Colts.
news.head: Cyrus Allen entirely uninvolved Sunday
news.impact: The rookie saw very little involvement for a second-straight game on Sunday night, which makes him unlikely to be productive for the foreseeable future. Fantasy managers should feel comfortable dropping him in favor of someone who has been getting more work for the first couple games of the season.

news.body: Cyrus Allen did not haul in his lone target in Monday night's 31-10 win over the Denver Broncos.
news.head: Cyrus Allen held catchless in win Monday
news.impact: The rookie was silent in his NFL debut on Monday, being held without a catch in the team's big win over the Broncos. They didn't need to pass much in this matchup, so it's possible that he will improve and play better in closer games moving forward. Still, this was a discouraging debut from a utilization standpoint, and fantasy managers shouldn't have high expectations for him for the foreseeable future.

news.body: Cyrus Allen returned to participating in 11-on-11s on Monday.
news.head: Cyrus Allen participates in 11-on-11s Monday
news.impact: It was the first time in training camp both Allen and Rashee Rice participated in 11-on-11s on the same day.

news.body: Cyrus Allen (shin) is back at practice on Friday, nearly a week after he suffered a bruised shin.
news.head: Cyrus Allen (shin) back at practice on Friday
news.impact: Allen was the talk of Chiefs training camp this offseason, and now the team gets him back. He will look to crack the lineup and make some noise come go time, but for now he’s just a late round dart in deep leagues at best.

news.body: Darius Cooper brought down 2-of-3 targets for 71 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 19-17 loss to the Jaguars.
news.head: Darius Cooper finds the end zone again in Week 5
news.impact: With DeVonta Smith (hamstring) missing each of the last two games, Cooper has now hit paydirt three times over the last two weeks and four times this season. The second-year pro is certainly proving himself as a big-play option for QB Jalen Hurts, but Cooper is still limited in the volume of targets thrown his way.

news.body: Darius Cooper hauled in 3-of-7 targets for 33 yards and two touchdowns in Sunday's 24-20 loss to the Los Angeles Rams.
news.head: Darius Cooper hauls in two touchdowns in loss Sunday
news.impact: Cooper was one of the lone bright spots on Philadelphia's offense on Sunday. He caught both of the team's passing touchdowns against the Rams, although he was only able to rack up 33 yards in the process. Fantasy managers shouldn't expect him to be a good fantasy option moving forward, however, especially with DeVonta Smith (hamstring) set to make his return to the lineup at some point.

news.body: Darius Cooper caught three of his five targets for 33 yards in a 24-17 loss to the Commanders in Week 18.
news.head: Darius Cooper hauls in three balls in Week 18
news.impact: Cooper turned in season-highs across the board with the Eagles resting several key starters on offense, including A.J. Brown. He will go back to a depth role next week in a Wild Card matchup against the 49ers.

news.body: The Eagles activated WR Darius Cooper from injured reserve.
news.head: Darius Cooper (shoulder) activated from IR
news.impact: Cooper had been designated to return earlier this week. He will be active on Sunday.

news.body: Darnell Mooney did not catch either of his two targets in the Giants 34-27 loss against the Saints.
news.head: Darnell Mooney does not catch pass Sunday
news.impact: Mooney had one carry for 20 yards. He remains off the fantasy radar.

news.body: Darnell Mooney (neck) was upgraded to a full participant at practice on Thursday.
news.head: Darnell Mooney (neck) upgraded to full participant Thursday
news.impact: The veteran was able to practice in a full capacity on Thursday, despite being limited by a neck issue on Wednesday. He should play in Week 6 but will continue to be irrelevant from a fantasy perspective moving forward.

news.body: Darnell Mooney was limited in practice on Wednesday.
news.head: Darnell Mooney (neck) limited in practice Wednesday
news.impact: Mooney remains off the fantasy radar in his current role.

news.body: Darnell Mooney caught two of his seven targets for 14 yards in the Giants' 27-27 tie with the Washington Commanders in Week 5.
news.head: Darnell Mooney quiet in Week 5 tie
news.impact: Mooney has underwhelmed to begin the season in the New York offense, finishing with less than 50 receiving yards in each of the first five contests. The wideout can be left off rosters in all formats ahead of a Week 6 contest against the New Orleans Saints.

news.body: Davante Adams caught five of his seven targets for 51 yards and two touchdowns in a 37-34 overtime loss to the Bills in Week 5.
news.head: Davante Adams brings in two TD passes in Week 5
news.impact: Adams found the end zone twice in the high-scoring loss on Monday night. He kicked off the scoring for LA with a four-yard grab in the second quarter and later came back to add a five-yard catch for a score. Adams now has 27 catches for 441 yards and four touchdowns through five games for the Rams. He will be a solid WR2 in Week 6 vs. the Cardinals.

news.body: Davante Adams is off the injury report for Monday's game against the Bills.
news.head: Davante Adams off injury report Monday
news.impact: Adams received a rest day in practice during the week. He'll remain a WR2 play for fantasy managers.

news.body: Davante Adams (rest) did not take part in practice on Thursday.
news.head: Davante Adams (rest) doesn't practice Thursday
news.impact: The Rams gave Adams the day off as a veteran rest day on Thursday. He should be back at practice on Friday and should be a full go for Monday night, looking to bounce back after an underwhelming performance in Week 4.

news.body: Davante Adams hauled in 4-of-9 targets for just 32 yards in Sunday's 24-20 win over the Philadelphia Eagles.
news.head: Davante Adams disappoints in win Sunday
news.impact: Adams was red-hot coming into this game, but he disappointed against the Eagles by catching just four of his nine targets for a measly 32 yards. He is no longer the top wideout on the team with Puka Nacua back in the lineup and healthy, so he will likely revert to being a boom-or-bust fantasy option on a week-to-week basis moving forward.

news.body: Deebo Samuel Sr. has been ruled out for Monday's game against the Commanders.
news.head: Deebo Samuel Sr. (hamstring) ruled out Monday
news.impact: Samuel will miss at least one game as expected. He remains week-to-week.

news.body: Deebo Samuel Sr. did not practice on Friday.
news.head: Deebo Samuel Sr. (hamstring) misses practice Friday
news.impact: Samuel is likely to miss at least one game. He remains week-to-week.

news.body: 49ers head coach Kyle Shanahan said Deebo Samuel would be an IR consideration but they’re going to hold off because of the bye in Week 8.
news.head: Deebo Samuel Sr. (hamstring) expected to avoid IR
news.impact: Samuel will likely remain sidelined through the bye week for San Francisco. He is week-to-week.

news.body: Deebo Samuel Sr. (hamstring) is expected to miss several weeks according to Ian Rapoport.
news.head: Deebo Samuel Sr. (hamstring) to miss several weeks
news.impact: Samuel Sr. exited Sunday’s win over the Seahawks after suffering the hamstring pull and is still scheduled for an MRI per previous reports, joining an extensive list of playmakers out of the lineup for head coach Kyle Shanahan as the season continues.

news.body: DeMario Douglas caught 7-of-8 targets for 86 yards and a touchdown in a 26-19 win over the Jets.
news.head: DeMario Douglas finds the end zone in Week 6 win
news.impact: Douglas led the team in receptions and receiving yards and found the end zone for the second straight game. If Rome Doubs (shoulder) is forced to miss any time, Douglas will likely see an increase in playing time. The Patriots take on the Bears Thursday.

news.body: DeMario Douglas caught 4-of-5 targets for 65 yards and two touchdowns in the Patriots win over Las Vegas.
news.head: DeMario Douglas hits pay dirt twice in Week 5 win
news.impact: Douglas found the end zone on receptions of eight and 35-yards, accounting for his first scores of the season. Douglas has an opportunity to become a key component of the offense with AJ Brown and Mack Hollins on injured reserve. Douglas and the Patriots will take on the Jets in Week 6.

news.body: DeMario Douglas caught 2-of-3 targets for 15 yards in the Patriots win over the Bills.
news.head: DeMario Douglas held to two receptions in Week 4
news.impact: Douglas continues to see limited targets in the Patriots' offense. Fantasy managers should feel comfortable leaving him on the waiver wire heading into Week 5.

news.body: DeMario Douglas caught 1-of-5 targets for 38 yards in Sunday's 35-6 loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars.
news.head: DeMario Douglas catches one pass in loss Sunday
news.impact: Douglas had a tough time connecting with QB Drake Maye on Sunday, catching just one of his five targets for a 38-yard gain. He will continue to see a solid amount of targets on a week-to-week basis moving forward but carries very little fantasy upside for the foreseeable future.

news.body: Cleveland Browns rookie wide receiver Denzel Boston logged a season low in receptions (one) with 15 yards in a Week 6 win over Baltimore.
news.head: Denzel Boston logs one catch in Week 6
news.impact: Boston has been a high point for Cleveland's offense, recording 40+ yards in the first five games to open his career. The rookie was still involved, earning five targets, though the opportunities did not translate into production. He should have another opportunity for a spike week against Tennessee in Week 7.

news.body: Denzel Boston (foot) is good to go for Sunday's game against the Baltimore Ravens.
news.head: Denzel Boston (foot) good to go for Sunday
news.impact: The rookie will be good to go on Sunday, despite dealing with a foot injury at practice throughout the week. He has been good through the first five weeks of the season and can safely be started in most league formats at this point.

news.body: Denzel Boston (foot) was limited at practice again on Thursday.
news.head: Denzel Boston (foot) limited again Thursday
news.impact: The rookie was limited for a second-straight practice on Thursday due to a nagging foot injury that he's dealing with. It looks like he will be available to play through it in Week 6, however, and fantasy managers should feel comfortable starting him if he doesn't carry an injury designation heading into the weekend.

news.body: Denzel Boston was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
news.head: Denzel Boston (foot) limited in practice Wednesday
news.impact: Boston should still be good to go for Sunday's game against the Ravens. His status is still worth monitoring in practice.

news.body: Devaughn Vele caught 3-of-6 targets for 42 yards in the Saints 34-27 win over the Giants.
news.head: Devaughn Vele totals 42 yards Sunday
news.impact: Vele was the second-leading receiver on the day for New Orleans. He is a borderline flex play in games where the passing volume is low for the Saints.

news.body: Devaughn Vele caught four of his six targets for 26 yards in the Saints' 23-13 Week 5 loss to the Minnesota Vikings.
news.head: Devaughn Vele bottled up in Week 5 loss
news.impact: Vele has made an inconsistent impact in the New Orleans passing attack, finishing with under 40 receiving yards in two of his last three contests. The wideout will look to get back on track for head coach Kellen Moore in Week 6 against the New York Giants.

news.body: Devaughn Vele caught 6-of-9 targets for 54 yards and a touchdown in Monday night's 45-24 loss to the Atlanta Falcons.
news.head: Devaughn Vele finds end zone Monday
news.impact: Vele's strong start to the season continued on Monday night. He caught six passes for 54 yards over the course of the game, one of which he was able to take to the house for a touchdown. He will continue to have solid week-to-week upside until Jordyn Tyson (hamstring) is back in the lineup for the Saints.

news.body: Devaughn Vele caught 3-of-6 targets for 39 yards in the Saints 35-27 loss against the Raiders on Sunday.
news.head: Devaughn Vele catches three passes Sunday
news.impact: Vele was relatively quiet for most of the afternoon. It was Chris Olave and the tight ends who dominated on the day for New Orleans. He remains an upside flex play heading into next week against the Falcons.

news.body: DeVonta Smith is off the injury report for Sunday's game against the Panthers.
news.head: DeVonta Smith (hamstring/toe) off injury report Sunday
news.impact: Smith was able to end the week with a full practice on Friday. He'll be a WR2 play with Tanner McKee behind center for the Eagles.

news.body: DeVonta Smith (hamstring/toe) was officially a limited participant at practice on Thursday.
news.head: DeVonta Smith (hamstring/toe) officially limited Thursday
news.impact: At first it looked like Smith was absent from Thursday's practice, but he turned out to be a limited participant. He's dealing with two separate injuries still, so it's very possible that he will be sidelined in Week 6, which would leave Dallas Goedert with more work than usual against the Panthers.

news.body: DeVonta Smith (hamstring) is not at practice on Thursday.
news.head: DeVonta Smith (hamstring) not at practice Thursday
news.impact: Yet another missed practice for the star wideout. He will have to practice on Friday in order to have a decent shot at playing on Sunday. If he misses another game, Dontayvion Wicks and Makai Lemon will headline the Eagles receiver group with Tanner McKee now at QB with Jalen Hurts ruled out.

news.body: DeVonta Smith did not practice on Wednesday.
news.head: DeVonta Smith (hamstring) misses practice Wednesday
news.impact: Smith is continuing to work his way ban from a hamstring injury. His status is uncertain for Sunday's game against the Panthers.

news.body: DJ Moore (shoulder) is inactive for Week 6 for the Buffalo Bills against the Las Vegas Raiders.
news.head: DJ Moore (shoulder) inactive for Week 6
news.impact: Moore will be sidelined for the second consecutive week as the wideout continues to battle through a shoulder injury. Keon Coleman and Khalil Shakir will see increased targets in Moore’s absence against the Raiders Sunday.

news.body: DJ Moore was in a non-contact jersey in practice on Friday.
news.head: DJ Moore (shoulder) in non-contact jersey Friday in practice
news.impact: Moore returned to practice, but in limited fashion. His status will need to be monitored on the official injury report.

news.body: DJ Moore (shoulder) missed another practice session on Thursday.
news.head: DJ Moore (shoulder) misses another practice Thursday
news.impact: Moore was sidelined for a second-straight practice on Thursday. The team continues to hold him out due to a nagging shoulder issue, and it remains to be seen if it will affect his availability for Week 6. If it does, fantasy managers should expect more work for Keon Coleman against the Raiders as a result.

news.body: DJ Moore (shoulder) did not take part in Buffalo's practice on Wednesday.
news.head: DJ Moore (shoulder) doesn't practice Wednesday
news.impact: Moore was sidelined at practice on Wednesday. The team held him out due to a shoulder injury that has been bothering him for a while, but it seems likely that he will return to practice on Thursday and play through it in Week 6, assuming he doesn't suffer any setbacks throughout the week.

news.body: DK Metcalf caught 11-of-15 targets for 93 yards in the Steelers 26-19 win over the Buccaneers.
news.head: DK Metcalf hauls in 11 passes Sunday
news.impact: Metcalf took over late as he totaled 12 targets in the fourth quarter and overtime period alone. He'll remain in the WR2/WR3 range with both Michael Pittman Jr. and Roman Wilson on IR.

news.body: DK Metcalf is off the injury report for Sunday's game against the Buccaneers.
news.head: DK Metcalf (illness) off injury report Sunday
news.impact: Metcalf had been listed as questionable with an illness. He'll be good to go with the Steelers wide receiver room depleted.

news.body: DK Metcalf (illness) is now questionable to play in Sunday's game against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.
news.head: DK Metcalf (illness) now questionable to play Sunday
news.impact: Metcalf is a new addition to Pittsburgh's injury report, being listed with an illness that left him sidelined at practice on Friday. He's now considered questionable to play heading into the weekend, and although it seems more likely than not that he will suit up, fantasy managers should still keep close tabs on all updates about his health over the next couple of days.

news.body: DK Metcalf caught three of four targets for 12 yards in the Steelers' 34-22 win over the Colts on Sunday.
news.head: DK Metcalf quiet in Week 5 win
news.impact: Metcalf took a backseat in this game to, well, most everyone on the Steelers. It's a far cry from his big game against the Browns, but that's pretty much who Metcalf is at this point in his career: a boom-bust type player.

news.body: Dontayvion Wicks (hamstring) did not take part in Philadelphia's practice on Thursday.
news.head: Dontayvion Wicks (hamstring) doesn't practice Thursday
news.impact: Wicks was not able to practice on Thursday. He's managing some kind of a hamstring issue and seems to be trending the wrong way for Week 6. Look for rookie Makai Lemon to see more work if Wicks is out this week, although neither of them should be started in this matchup against the Panthers either way.

news.body: Dontayvion Wicks was limited in practice on Wednesday.
news.head: Dontayvion Wicks (hamstring) limited in practice Wednesday
news.impact: Wicks is on the injury report with a hamstring issue. He should be good to go for Sunday's game against the Panthers.

news.body: Dontayvion Wicks secured 5-of-8 targets for 63 yards in Sunday's 19-17 loss to the Jaguars.
news.head: Dontayvion Wicks hauls in five passes Sunday
news.impact: With top wideout DeVonta Smith (hamstring) out for the second straight week, Wicks saw a season high in targets Sunday. He also tied a season high with five receptions and crossed the 60-yard mark for the third time in the first five weeks. Wicks is at least in the flex conversation for standard leagues right now.

news.body: Dontayvion Wicks is off the injury report for Sunday's game against the Jaguars.
news.head: Dontayvion Wicks (hamstring) off injury report Sunday
news.impact: Wicks will be good to go despite being added to the injury report on Thursday. He'll be a WR3 for fantasy managers.

news.body: Drake London hauled in four of his team-leading 10 targets for 62 yards in the Falcons' 31-23 Week 6 loss to the Chicago Bears.
news.head: Drake London sees 10 targets in Week 6 loss to Bears
news.impact: London continues to make the most of his role as the primary option in an inconsistent Atlanta passing attack, registering 10 or more targets in three of the last four contests. The wideout will look to make a more explosive impact in a Week 7 matchup against the San Francisco 49ers.

news.body: Drake London caught 7-of-11 targets for 118 yards in Sunday's 30-23 OT loss to the Ravens.
news.head: Drake London eclipses 100 yards in Sunday's loss
news.impact: London went over 100 yards for the second time in three weeks Sunday night, and he only missed the mark by four yards in Week 4. Surprisingly, London has still yet to find the end zone on any of his 27 grabs this season. London has looked nothing less than a WR1 with Michael Penix at QB for the Falcons. Unfortunately, Penix (ribs) is now dealing with another injury.

news.body: Drake London hauled in 5-of-6 targets for 96 yards in Monday night's 45-24 win over the New Orleans Saints.
news.head: Drake London leads team in receiving Monday
news.impact: Most of Atlanta's receiving options didn't see much work on Monday with how dominant the team's running game was, but London was the exception to that. He fell just four yards shy of a 100-yard outing against the Saints and finished with another good performance for fantasy managers. He has looked great ever since QB Michael Penix Jr. took the starting job for the Falcons, so he should continue to be a great fantasy asset for the foreseeable future.

news.body: Drake London caught 9 of 10 targets for 194 yards in the Falcons' 35-14 win over the Packers on Thursday.
news.head: Drake London goes for 194 yards in win over Green Bay
news.impact: London was fantastic in this game, spurred on by the return of Michael Penix. When Penix has been at the helm of the offense, London has been among the best fantasy producers in the game, and it showed once again on Thursday. He should be a locked in starter whenever Penix is playing.

news.body: Efton Chism III caught 5-of-6 targets for 57 yards in the Patriots win over the Raiders. He added two rushing yards on one carry.
news.head: Efton Chism III hauls in five passes in Week 5 win
news.impact: Chism led the team in targets with six, setting an new season high in targets, yards, and receptions. With Mack Hollins and AJ Brown on injured reserve, Chism appears to be carving out a role in the offense.

news.body: Efton Chism III caught 2-of-4 targets for 42 yards and a touchdown in the Patriots win over the Bills.
news.head: Efton Chism III finds the end zone in Week 4 win
news.impact: Chism made an impressive 23-yard touchdown reception late in the fourth quarter to give the Patriots the lead and the win Sunday. His two receptions and 42 yards establish new season highs, but Chism could be asked to do more in Week 5 if Mack Hollins (calf) is unable to suit up against Las Vegas.

news.body: Efton Chism III caught both of his targets for 40 yards and a touchdown in the Patriots 42-10 win over the Jets.
news.head: Efton Chism III finds the end zone in Week 17
news.impact: Chism caught a 10-yard pass for a touchdown in the third quarter, accounting for his first career score. The Patriots were depleted at wide receiver, giving Chism an opportunity to play on offense. The rookie will look to build on this performance in Week 18 against Miami.

news.body: Efton Chism III is inactive for Week 1 for the New England Patriots against the Las Vegas Raiders.
news.head: Efton Chism III inactive for Week 1
news.impact: Chism III is a healthy inactive for head coach Mike Vrabel against the Raiders and is little more than a depth option in the New England offense when active to begin the season.

news.body: Emeka Egbuka caught six of nine targets for 38 yards, also running once for a 14-yard score in Tampa Bay's 24-16 win over the Cowboys.
news.head: Emeka Egbuka runs in touchdown in win
news.impact: Egbuka had a long of 21 yards, meaning his five other receptions amounted to just 17 total yards. He was still the highest-targeted Bucs receiver on the night, with no other Tampa player garnering more than four targets. He doesn't have quite the same appeal he might have if a veteran were tossing him the ball, but Daniels has shown competence so far in his two starts while QB Baker Mayfield recovers from injury, and should only get better.

news.body: Emeka Egbuka caught two of his four targets for 13 yards in a 17-14 loss to the Packers in Week 4.
news.head: Emeka Egbuka held to 13 yards in Week 4 loss
news.impact: Egbuka was quiet with rookie Jalon Daniels making his NFL debut at quarterback for the Bucs. Daniels seemed to key in on Cade Otton and Chris Godwin when dropping back to pass, leaving Egbuka with his least productive performance of the season. Overall, Egbuka has 15 catches for 154 yards and one touchdown through four games. Hard to trust without Baker Mayfield under center, Egbuka will be a flex option in fantasy in Week 5 vs. the Cowboys.

news.body: Emeka Egbuka caught 5-of-9 targets for 62 yards in the Buccaneers 23-16 loss against the Vikings on Sunday.
news.head: Emeka Egbuka totals 62 yards Sunday
news.impact: Egbuka was the leading receiver for Tampa Bay on the day. He has still yet to have one of his huge explosive games. The status of Baker Mayfield will need to be monitored after he left the game late with a dislocated thumb.

news.body: Emeka Egbuka caught 3-of-5 targets for 16 yards and a touchdown in the Buccaneers 23-19 loss against the Browns.
news.head: Emeka Egbuka has touchdown salvage performance Sunday
news.impact: It would have been a disastrous afternoon for Egbuka if it weren't for a touchdown he hauled in. He'll remain a WR2 play next week against the Vikings.

news.body: Garrett Wilson caught 4-of-6 targets for 44 yards in the Jets' 26-19 loss to the Patriots.
news.head: Garrett Wilson hauls in four passes in Week 6 loss
news.impact: Wilson turned in his second lowest output of the season in the loss Sunday. Despite the performance Sunday, Wilson remains the top fantasy option heading into a Week 7 matchup with Miami.

news.body: Garrett Wilson caught seven of his 11 targets for 104 yards and one touchdown in a 17-12 win over the Browns in Week 5.
news.head: Garrett Wilson finds the end zone in Week 5
news.impact: Wilson easily paced the Jets in receiving, hauling in 104 of the team's 182 passing yards in the close win. He found the end zone on a 32-yard strike from Geno Smith in the first quarter. Wilson has now caught 31 passes for 374 yards and three touchdowns across five games. He will be on the WR1/WR2 borderline in Week 6 against the Patriots.

news.body: Garrett Wilson caught three of his four targets for 27 yards in a 23-12 loss to the Bears in Week 4.
news.head: Garrett Wilson held to 27 yards in Week 4
news.impact: Wilson and the Jets struggled to get anything going in the loss to Chicago. The Jets were held to just 119 passing yards, with most of the damage coming via a 58-yard touchdown pass to Isaiah Williams. Wilson has caught 24 passes for 270 yards and two touchdowns through four games. He will be a low-end WR1/high-end WR2 in fantasy in a Week 5 home matchup against the Browns.

news.body: Garrett Wilson caught 10-of-13 targets for 107 yards and a touchdown in a 31-24 loss to the Lions.
news.head: Garrett Wilson hauls in 10 passes in Week 3 loss
news.impact: Wilson caught a 24-yard strike from Geno Smith in the fourth quarter to tie the game. Fantasy managers will want to monitor Wilson's status early in the week as he did exit with an injury on the final drive. Wilson and the Jets will take on the Bears in Week 4.

news.body: George Pickens caught 9 of 13 targets for 130 yards and a touchdown in the Cowboys' 24-16 loss to the Bucs on Thursday.
news.head: George Pickens goes off against Tampa secondary
news.impact: Pickens had himself a night on Thursday, partially spurred on by the loss of CeeDee Lamb for a good portion of the game. Pickens was bound to connect with Dak Prescott on a deep shot at some point, given all the different times they had attempted to do so before. He had a nice touchdown grab with his typical no-separation, "Moss" -ing style. Pickens has been an ok asset for fantasy, but certainly not the WR1 like he was last year.

news.body: George Pickens caught 2-of-3 targets for 75 yards in the Cowboys 34-30 win over the Texans.
news.head: George Pickens totals 75 yards Sunday
news.impact: Pickens had a huge 53-yard reception salvage his day. It was the CeeDee Lamb show on Sunday. Pickens remains a WR2 play heading into Thursday’s game against the Buccaneers.

news.body: George Pickens caught seven of his 11 targets for 82 yards in a 34-31 loss to the Ravens in Brazil in Week 3.
news.head: George Pickens draws 11 targets in Week 3
news.impact: Pickens led the way with his 11 targets while finishing second behind CeeDee Lamb in receiving yards. The veteran wideout has now caught 16 passes for 150 scoreless yards through three games this season. He will be on the WR1/WR2 borderline in Week 4 in a matchup against a tough Texans defense.

news.body: George Pickens caught 6-of-8 targets for 40 yards in the Cowboys in a win over the Commanders.
news.head: George Pickens hauls in six passes in Week 2
news.impact: Pickens had a much needed bounce back performance after tallying just three receptions. Although Pickens has not found the endzone yet this season, the increase in targets and receptions over the first week is a strong sign that Pickens will remain a factor in this offense. The Cowboys will take on the Ravens in Week 3.

news.body: Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy said 'football comes easy' to Germie Bernard.
news.head: Germie Bernard draws praise from HC Mike McCarthy
news.impact: "He's acclimated very well to the offense, can play all three positions, and sticks his nose in there," McCarthy said. "I've been very impressed." Bernard is set to step into a bigger role with Roman Wilson week-to-week.

news.body: Germie Bernard caught six of nine targets for 80 yards in the Steelers' 34-22 win over the Colts.
news.head: Germie Bernard has breakout game against Colts
news.impact: Bernard benefited from the absence of Michael Pittman and Roman Wilson, with the former on IR and the latter sustaining a finger injury after attempting a catch. Bernard had some issues with drops, but he showed potential for what he could do with an expanded workload. Look for him to have a healthy target share yet again against Tampa Bay next week.

news.body: Germie Bernard caught his lone target for 14 yards in a 30-27 win over the Bengals.
news.head: Germie Bernard held to one target in Week 3
news.impact: Bernard saw his target share free fall to just one target after seeing eight last week against the Patriots. The 22-year-old should remain out of lineups until us usage becomes more clear.

news.body: Steelers WR Germie Bernard caught 4-of-8 targets for 35 yards in the Steelers' 20-3 loss to the Patriots.
news.head: Germie Bernard leads team in receiving yards in Week 2
news.impact: Bernard saw an increase in playing time with Michael Pittman (ankle) unavailable for Week 2. The rookie wide receiver did have a key drop that lead to a Patriots interception. Bernard will look to build on this performance in Week 3 against the Bengals.

news.body: Isaiah Williams caught one of his two targets for a 16-yard gain in a 17-12 win over the Browns in Week 5.
news.head: Isaiah Williams catches one pass in Week 5
news.impact: Williams was quiet in the close win, hauling in just one pass. With Garrett Wilson accounting for 104 of the team's 182 passing yards, there wasn't much else to go around to the other pass-catchers. Williams will be a low-end flex against the Patriots in Week 6.

news.body: Isaiah Williams caught two of his three targets for 73 yards and a touchdown in a 23-12 loss to the Bears in Week 4.
news.head: Isaiah Williams finds the end zone in Week 4
news.impact: Williams was one of the few bright spots for the Jets in the loss as he hauled in a 58-yard touchdown pass from Geno Smith in the fourth quarter. Williams now has 10 catches for 135 yards and one touchdown through four games. If Adonai Mitchell (finger) misses a third straight game in Week 5 vs. the Browns, Williams will be on the flex radar in fantasy.

news.body: Isaiah Williams caught 1-of-2 targets for 21 yards in a 31-24 loss to the Lions.
news.head: Isaiah Williams hauls in one pass in Week 3 loss
news.impact: Williams saw a big drop in his target share after logging six targets in Week 2. The performance is disappointing considering the Jets were without Adonai Mitchell. Williams and the Jets will look to bounce back against the Bears in Week 4.

news.body: Isaiah Williams hauled in all six of his targets for 34 yards while also rushing once for 14 yards in the Jets' 20-17 loss to the Green Bay Packers in Week 2.
news.head: Isaiah Williams sees seven touches in Week 2
news.impact: Williams made the most of increased involvement in an underwhelming passing attack, finishing tied for first in receptions in the loss. The wideout remains difficult to trust as another inconsistent pass-catching option ahead of a favorable Week 3 contest against the Detroit Lions.

news.body: Jahan Dotson hauled in three of his five targets for 87 yards and one touchdown in the Falcons' 31-23 Week 6 loss to the Chicago Bears.
news.head: Jahan Dotson finds end zone in Week 6 loss
news.impact: Dotson has made the most of his opportunities in the Atlanta passing offense of late, finishing with over 50 receiving yards in each of his last three contests. The wideout will look to offer head coach another stable pass-catching option moving forward, with a Week 7 contest against the San Francisco 49ers up next.

news.body: Jahan Dotson caught 2-of-4 targets for 54 yards in Sunday's 30-23 OT loss to the Ravens.
news.head: Jahan Dotson finishes with 54 receiving yards in Week 5
news.impact: Dotson made a couple of big grabs in Sunday's game, but he remained no higher than the fourth option in the Falcons' passing attack. Dotson is averaging 18.6 yards per reception and caught his only touchdown so far this season in Week 4. That TD came off the arm of Michael Penix, who is now dealing with a rib injury.

news.body: Jahan Dotson hauled in 2-of-3 targets for 54 yards and a touchdown in Monday night's 45-24 win over the New Orleans Saints.
news.head: Jahan Dotson hauls in touchdown Monday
news.impact: Dotson contributed well in Week 4, logging over 50 yards and getting into the end zone in a blowout win over the Saints. This was a good game for the veteran, but fantasy managers shouldn't expect him to have consistent value moving forward.

news.body: The Falcons signed WR Jahan Dotson to a two-year contract worth $15 million.
news.head: Jahan Dotson signs two-year deal with Falcons
news.impact: Dotson will have a chance to earn his way into the role held by Darnell Mooney. He had a limited role in Philadelphia behind AJ Brown and DeVonta Smith. He'll be a WR3 at best from a fantasy football perspective, but more likely in the WR4 range.

news.body: Jakobi Meyers caught 5-of-10 targets for 83 yards in a 34-31 loss to Houston.
news.head: Jakobi Meyers hauls in five passes in Week 6 loss
news.impact: Meyers lead the team in catches and receiving Sunday, falling just one target behind Parker Washington for the team lead. The veteran turned in his best performance of the season so far and will look to build on that after their bye week in Week 7.

news.body: Jakobi Meyers caught 2-of-3 targets for 37 yards in Sunday's 19-17 win over the Eagles.
news.head: Jakobi Meyers finishes with two grabs in Sunday's win
news.impact: Meyers continues to be a reliable receiver for QB Trevor Lawrence, but he has now finished with three or fewer grabs and no more than 40 yards in four of the first five games of the season. Meyers seems to be the third option in the passing game behind top wideout Parker Washington and TE Brenton Strange. Rookie Josh Cameron is on the ascent too.

news.body: Jakobi Meyers caught three passes for 33 yards in Sunday's 22-17 win over the Cincinnati Bengals.
news.head: Jakobi Meyers catches three passes Sunday
news.impact: The veteran wasn't able to do much of note on Sunday, finishing with just 33 yards in a narrow win over the Bengals. Fantasy managers shouldn't expect him to be relevant moving forward, however, especially with some tough matchups coming up for Jacksonville's offense over the next two weeks.

news.body: Jakobi Meyers (thumb) was listed as a limited participant at practice on Thursday.
news.head: Jakobi Meyers (thumb) listed as limited Thursday
news.impact: As expected, Meyers remained a limited participant for another practice on Thursday. He should be good to go for Sunday's game, however, assuming he doesn't suffer any setbacks between now and then.

news.body: The Cardinals signed WR Jalen Brooks to their active roster.
news.head: Jalen Brooks signs with Cardinals active roster
news.impact: Brooks had been on the practice squad for Arizona. He takes the roster spot of Andre Baccellia who was placed on IR.

news.body: The Cardinals elevated WR Jalen Brooks from the practice squad.
news.head: Jalen Brooks elevated to Cardinals' active roster
news.impact: Brooks will add depth to a banged up Cardinals wide receiver room. He remains off the fantasy radar.

news.body: The Cardinals signed WR Jalen Brooks to their practice squad.
news.head: Jalen Brooks signs with Cardinals practice squad
news.impact: Arizona had a spot open on its practice squad. Brooks will add depth to their wide receiver room.

news.body: The Cowboys placed WR Jalen Brooks on practice squad IR.
news.head: Jalen Brooks placed on practice squad IR
news.impact: Dallas signed DB Zion Childress to the practice squad as the corresponding move.

news.body: Carolina Panthers wide receiver Jalen Coker caught six passes for 97 yards while seeing a season-high 13 targets in Week 6.
news.head: Jalen Coker has game-high 97 yards vs. Eagles
news.impact: Coker has at least nine targets in every game he has finished this season, forming an impressive tandem with second-year star Tetairoa McMillan. He had two touchdowns in Week 1 and has not scored since, but Carolina's passing attack has been impressive, and more will come in the future.

news.body: Jalen Coker (quad) practiced in a full capacity again on Thursday.
news.head: Jalen Coker (quad) practices in full again Thursday
news.impact: As expected, Coker was able to log another full practice session on Thursday. He's expected to be close to full health for Sunday's game against the Eagles, in which case fantasy managers can feel comfortable starting him in that matchup.

news.body: Jalen Coker (quad) practiced in a full capacity on Wednesday.
news.head: Jalen Coker (quad) practices in full Wednesday
news.impact: Coker got healthy over the team's bye week last week and seems to be set to make in his return to the lineup in Week 6. He was able to log a full practice to start the week on Wednesday, so unless he suffers a setback throughout the week, fantasy managers should expect him to play and see a full workload against the Eagles on Sunday.

news.body: Panthers coach Dave Canales said Jalen Coker is “on track” to play in Carolina’s Week 6 game against the Eagles.
news.head: Jalen Coker (quad) remains on track to return in Week 6
news.impact: This confirms a previous report from Monday. He was spotted practicing on Tuesday.

news.body: Jalen Nailor (concussion) returned to practice for the Raiders on Thursday.
news.head: Jalen Nailor (concussion) returns to practice Thursday
news.impact: Nailor was able to practice in a limited fashion on Thursday, and his return is a good sign that he is trending in the right direction. If he's out for another game on Sunday, fantasy managers should expect more work for Tre Tucker against the Bills.

news.body: Jalen Nailor (concussion) missed Las Vegas' practice on Wednesday.
news.head: Jalen Nailor (concussion) misses practice Wednesday
news.impact: Nailor is still going through the NFL's concussion protocols and was left sidelined at practice on Wednesday as a result. He is expected to return to practice at some point this week, but it is unclear when that will be exactly or in what capacity. Tre Tucker will see more work if the veteran is sidelined again in Week 6.

news.body: Raiders coach Klint Kubiak confirmed that Jalen Nailor will return to practice this week.
news.head: Jalen Nailor (concussion) to return to practice this week
news.impact: Nailor has been in concussion protocol. He'll have a chance to return for Sunday's game against the Bills.

news.body: Jalen Nailor has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Patriots.
news.head: Jalen Nailor (concussion) ruled out Sunday
news.impact: Nailor will remain sidelined in concussion protocol.

news.body: Jalen Royals caught his only target for 11 yards in the Chiefs' 24-10 win over the Miami Dolphins in Week 3.
news.head: Jalen Royals sees one target in Week 3
news.impact: Royals remains minimally involved in the Kansas City offense early on, recording less than 15 receiving yards in each of his two contests. The wideout remains best left off rosters in all formats ahead of a Week 4 contest against the Las Vegas Raiders.

news.body: Chiefs head coach Andy Reid told reporters Jalen Royals received first-team reps in practice on Thursday.
news.head: Jalen Royals receives first-team reps Thursday
news.impact: There is an opening in the Chiefs wide receiver room with Rashee Rice away from the team. "With Rashee not here, it gives Jalen some great reps at the wide receiver position," Reid said. "He looks strong out here. Running well. It's great for him. It's great for him and the quarterbacks to see what he's all about."

news.body: Jalen Royals (knee) fully practiced for the Chiefs on Wednesday.
news.head: Jalen Royals (knee) fully practices Wednesday
news.impact: The rookie saw almost no action despite being active in Week 3, but it doesn't seem like his knee injury is still much of an issue, as he was a full participant in Friday's practice. The team is taking their time and letting him get up to speed, so we will probably see him get more involved as the season goes along.

news.body: Jalen Royals (knee) was upgraded to a full participant at practice on Thursday.
news.head: Jalen Royals (knee) upgraded to full participant Thursday
news.impact: The rookie will likely be available to play for the Chiefs on Sunday. He has been battling a knee injury recently, but was able to log a full practice session on Thursday, indicating that he is near full health at this point. It remains to be seen what his role will look like with Kansas City's offense to start out.

news.body: Ja'Marr Chase hauled in 6-of-10 targets for 77 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 31-24 win over the Miami Dolphins.
news.head: Ja'Marr Chase leads team in receiving Sunday
news.impact: Chase was able to clear the NFL's concussion protocols prior to game time on Sunday and looked great in Cincinnati's win over the Dolphins. He led the team in targets, receptions, and receiving yards, and he was also able to get into the end zone on one occasion. He is expected to continue to be a top-tier fantasy option over the rest of the regular season, after the team has their bye week in Week 6.

news.body: Ja’Marr Chase (concussion) is cleared to play for the Cincinnati Bengals against the Miami Dolphins Sunday.
news.head: Ja’Marr Chase (concussion) to play Sunday
news.impact: Chase was able to clear through concussion protocols ahead of the Week 5 contest, offering quarterback Joe Burrow both of his explosive pass-catching options along with Tee Higgins (groin/neck) against the Dolphins Sunday.

news.body: Bengals head coach Zac Taylor said Ja'Marr Chase remains in concussion protocol.
news.head: Ja'Marr Chase remains in concussion protocol
news.impact: Chase was in uniform during practice on Friday. He will have till Saturday to clear all protocols in time for Sunday.

news.body: Ja'Marr Chase is in uniform at practice on Friday.
news.head: Ja'Marr Chase (concussion) in uniform at practice Friday
news.impact: Chase was officially limited at practice on Thursday. He'll have till Saturday to clear concussion protocol in time for Sunday's game.

news.body: Jameson Williams caught 2-of-4 targets for 47 yards and two touchdowns in Sunday's 45-21 win over the Arizona Cardinals.
news.head: Jameson Williams scores twice in win Sunday
news.impact: Williams only caught two passes on Sunday, but he was able to get into the end zone on both of them, which left him with a great fantasy total in this win over the Cardinals. He is expected to continue to be a boom-or-bust fantasy option on a week-to-week basis moving forward.

news.body: Jameson Williams came up with 6-of-8 targets for 102 yards in Sunday's 32-26 loss to the Panthers.
news.head: Jameson Williams clears 100 yards in Week 4 loss
news.impact: After being held under 50 yards and no more than four grabs over the first three weeks of the season, Williams finally got going Sunday night. The big-play blazer had a long gain of 49 yards and averaged 17 yards on his half-dozen receptions. Williams should be viewed as an upside WR3 heading into Week 5.

news.body: Jameson Williams caught 4-of-4 targets for 49 yards in a 31-24 win over the Jets.
news.head: Jameson Williams hauls in four passes in Week 3 win
news.impact: Williams took a back seat in the offense Sunday with Amon-Ra St. Brown and Jahmyr Gibbs dominating the targets against the Jets. Williams will look to become more involved in the offense in a Week 4 matchup with the Panthers.

news.body: Jameson Williams caught 2-of-4 targets for 33 yards in Thursday night's 41-31 loss to the Buffalo Bills.
news.head: Jameson Williams underwhelming in loss Thursday
news.impact: Williams had another disappointing performance on Thursday night. He caught just two passes in this matchup against the Bills and was only able to turn that into 33 scoreless yards, leaving him with a poor fantasy total on the night. Fantasy managers should recognize his low week-to-week floor when determining whether or not to start him in any given game moving forward.

news.body: Jaxon Smith-Njigba caught 12 of 16 targets for 134 yards in the Seahawks' 17-14 overtime loss to the Broncos on Thursday.
news.head: Jaxon Smith-Njigba continues crazy start to season in loss to Denver
news.impact: JSN had himself a night against the Broncos' defense, though he got off to a quiet start. He has 717 yards through six games, a blistering pace of 2,031 receiving yards. He had almost 1,800 receiving yards last year, and if he can match or exceed that in 2026, it would be truly incredible.

news.body: Jaxon Smith-Njigba was upgraded to a full practice on Wednesday and has no injury designation for Thursday night.
news.head: Jaxon Smith-Njigba practices in full Wednesday, no injury designation
news.impact: JSN was initially listed as limited due to an ankle injury, but it looks like he will be a full go against Denver. Lock him into starting lineups.

news.body: Jaxon Smith-Njigba was listed as a limited practice participant on Tuesday’s estimated injury report.
news.head: Jaxon Smith-Njigba (ankle) limited on estimated practice report Tuesday
news.impact: Smith-Njigba got the same designation on Monday. He should be good to go for Thursday’s game against the Broncos.

news.body: Jaxon Smith-Njigba was listed as a limited participant on Monday's estimated injury report.
news.head: Jaxon Smith-Njigba (ankle) limited on estimated injury report Monday
news.impact: Smith-Njigba missed some time in Sunday's game after he twisted his ankle, but he was able to finish the game. He should be good to go on Thursday against the Broncos.

news.body: Jaylen Waddle caught four of seven targets for 24 yards in the Broncos' 17-14 win over the Seahawks on Thursday.
news.head: Jaylen Waddle disappoints in win over Seattle
news.impact: Waddle has been a disappointment this season, no way around it. He's not producing, so you can't start him, but you know the potential he holds, so you can't drop him. It's a tough situation for fantasy managers to be in, so do what is best for your roster. If you can afford to hold and not start Waddle, do so. But if you need help, Waddle could be a cut candidate.

news.body: Jaylen Waddle caught only 2-of-5 targets for 19 yards and gained nine yards on one carry in Sunday's 23-17 win over the Chargers.
news.head: Jaylen Waddle does little with three touches in Week 5 win
news.impact: Waddle has been on a production rollercoaster over his first five games with the Broncos, reflecting the inconsistency of the Denver passing attack overall. After catching five passes and scoring his first touchdown of the season in Week 4, Waddle got very little done in Week 5. It's been frustrating for fantasy managers to this point, but Waddle is the clear No. 1 WR for the Broncos and the potential for big numbers is there.

news.body: Jaylen Waddle caught five of his six targets for 35 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 24-14 loss to the San Francisco 49ers.
news.head: Jaylen Waddle scores touchdown in loss Sunday
news.impact: Waddle didn't put up many yards, but he saved his fantasy day with a 13-yard touchdown in the fourth quarter. He finished second on the team in receptions but was held to just 7.0 yards per catch. Waddle remains one of Denver's top options in the passing game and should continue to see enough targets to remain in fantasy lineups as a WR2.

news.body: Jaylen Waddle is off the injury report for Sunday's game against the 49ers.
news.head: Jaylen Waddle (foot) off injury report Sunday
news.impact: Waddle was seen in a walking boot after last Sunday's win. He will be a WR2 play for fantasy managers.

news.body: Jaylin Noel caught all four of his targets for 107 yards and a touchdown in the Texans' 34-31 win over Jacksonville.
news.head: Jaylin Noel finds the end zone in Week 6 win
news.impact: Noel found the end zone on a 13-yard connection from C.J Stroud in the third quarter. Noel has shown a positive rapport with Stroud, but will likely remain behind Nico Collins in the pass catcher pecking order for the duration of the season.

news.body: Jaylin Noel caught 5-of-5 targets for 41 yards and a touchdown in the Texans 26-3 win over the Titans.
news.head: Jaylin Noel hauls in five passes Sunday
news.impact: Noel tied Nico Collins for the team-high in receptions on the day. He has shown some flashes, but his role isn't consistent enough to put him on the fantasy radar.

news.body: Jaylin Noel caught 3-of-3 targets for 85 yards in the Texans 34-30 loss against the Cowboys.
news.head: Jaylin Noel totals 85 yards Sunday
news.impact: Noel had a huge catch of 52 yards downfield from C.J. Stroud. He remains an upside flex play for fantasy managers.

news.body: Jaylin Noel caught both of his targets for 17 yards in a 19-17 loss to the Colts.
news.head: Jaylin Noel hauls in two passes in Week 3
news.impact: Noel saw his target share drop from his five targets in Week 2. Fantasy managers can leave the 24-year-old on the waiver wire heading into Week 4.

news.body: Cleveland Browns wide receiver Jerry Jeudy caught four passes for a team-high 69 yards in a Week 6 win against Baltimore.
news.head: Jerry Jeudy paces Cleveland in yards in Week 6
news.impact: Jeudy had his biggest game of the season so far, catching every target for a season-high in yardage. His name has been thrown around in trade rumors after the Browns' rookie wideouts started strong, but he has value as the team's WR3, even if he is not a reliable fantasy producer.

news.body: The Browns are reportedly seeking a third or fourth-round pick for WR Jerry Jeudy.
news.head: Jerry Jeudy could be traded by Browns
news.impact: Jordan Schultz reported he's not sure they’ll be able to get it. Jeudy will be a player to monitor closer to the trade deadline.

news.body: Jerry Jeudy caught three of his seven targets for 19 yards in a 17-12 loss to the Jets in Week 5.
news.head: Jerry Jeudy catches three passes in Week 5
news.impact: Jeudy tied for the lead with seven targets, but he wasn't able to do much with the opportunities. The veteran wideout has been quiet through the first five games of the season, catching just eight passes for 81 yards. He will not be a recommended fantasy option in Week 6 against Baltimore

news.body: Jerry Jeudy caught all three of his targets in Thursday's 27-24 win over the Steelers.
news.head: Jerry Jeudy hauls in three passes Thursday night
news.impact: After catching no passes with just one target over the last two weeks, Jeudy got involved again on Thursday night. He was still targeted just three times while playing only 24 snaps. Jeudy should remain on the waiver wire in all but the deepest of fantasy leagues.

news.body: Jordan Addison (hamstring) is inactive for Week 5 for the Minnesota Vikings against the New Orleans Saints according to Tom Pelissero.
news.head: Jordan Addison (hamstring) inactive for Week 5
news.impact: Addison will not suit up after struggling to progress throughout the week for head coach Kevin O’Connell, while No. 1 wideout Justin Jefferson (ankle) is good to go for the Week 5 contest against the Saints.

news.body: Jordan Addison (hamstring) is not expected to play for the Minnesota Vikings against the New Orleans Saints Sunday according to Jeff Darlington.
news.head: Jordan Addison (hamstring) not expected to play Sunday
news.impact: Addison struggled to progress throughout the week for head coach Kevin O’Connell, leaving the Minnesota passing attack without a primary pass-catching option against the Saints Sunday.

news.body: Jordan Addison is listed as questionable for Sunday’s game against the Saints.
news.head: Jordan Addison (hamstring) listed questionable Sunday
news.impact: Addison was able to practice again on Friday. He should be on the favorable side of questionable heading into Sunday, but his status will still need to be monitored closer to kickoff.

news.body: Jordan Addison was at practice again on Friday.
news.head: Jordan Addison (hamstring) at practice Friday
news.impact: Addison returned to a limited practice on Thursday. He should be on track to playing on Sunday against the Saints.

news.body: Saints coach Kellen Moore said, “not right now" when asked if Jordyn Tyson could practice this week.
news.head: Jordyn Tyson (hamstring) not ready to practice yet
news.impact: Moore adds that Tyson is “progressing well." He remains week-to-week for now.

news.body: Saints coach Kellen Moore said he doesn’t expect Jordyn Tyson to return to practice this week.
news.head: Jordyn Tyson (hamstring) will not return to practice this week
news.impact: Moore did add that Tyson is progressing well. He remains week-to-week.

news.body: Jordyn Tyson (hamstring) is still considered “weeks away” from returning from IR due to his hamstring injury, despite being eligible to return at the conclusion of Week 4. It appears Week 7 is the earliest we could see him return, but the Saints bye is the following week, so Week 9 is sounding more realistic.
news.head: Jordyn Tyson (hamstring) still ‘weeks away’ from return
news.impact: It’s a tough blow for Tyson’s stock and for fantasy managers who have held on to him this long. Tyson has loads of promise and could unlock something for a Saints offense that’s already looking good. However, we will have to wait several more weeks to see him on the field, and in his absence, Juwan Johnson and Devaughn Vele will continue to be viable starts.

news.body: The Saints placed Jordyn Tyson on injured reserve.
news.head: Jordyn Tyson (hamstring) placed on IR
news.impact: Tyson is expected to miss roughly two months with a hamstring injury. He has been dealing with hamstring issues since college at Arizona State.

news.body: Josh Cameron secured 3-of-6 targets for 43 yards in Sunday's 19-17 win over the Eagles.
news.head: Josh Cameron hauls in three passes Sunday
news.impact: Cameron has quickly carved himself out a role among Jaguars pass catchers. The sixth-round rookie out of Baylor has now come up with 5-of-8 targets for 85 yards over the last two weeks, including gains of 29 and 32 yards. Cameron set new career highs in receptions and targets in Week 5, outpacing both Jakobi Meyers and Brian Thomas Jr.

news.body: Josh Cameron caught both of his targets for 20 yards and a touchdown in the Jaguars' 34-10 win over the Browns on Sunday.
news.head: Josh Cameron snags touchdown in NFL debut
news.impact: The rookie receiver had the wonderful experience of catching a touchdown in his first-ever regular-season game. However, it's hard to take much from it for fantasy, as the Jaguars' passing attack is incredibly spread out and Cameron is buried on the depth chart. His usage might trend up as the season goes along, and he's at least a name to monitor for dynasty formats. But don't expect anything big in the short term.

news.body: The Jacksonville Jaguars have selected WR Josh Cameron with the No. 191 overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft.
news.head: Josh Cameron selected No. 191 by Jacksonville Jaguars
news.impact: The Jacksonville Jaguars have a plethora of wide receivers after investing first-round picks in back-to-back years on Brian Thomas Jr. and Travis Hunter. They also have Jakobi Meyers and Parker Washington, leaving little to no opportunity for Josh Cameron to have a fantasy impact without significant injuries to the team's wide receiver corps.

news.body: Baylor WR Josh Cameron is on track to be fully healthy by rookie minicamp.
news.head: Josh Cameron (calf) on track to be fully healthy for rookie minicamp
news.impact: Cameron suffered a calf strain at the Combine. He has spent time with 15 teams on visits, including the Falcons most recently.

news.body: Josh Downs caught four of eight targets for 40 yards in the Colts' 26-20 loss to the Titans on Sunday. He also ran the ball once for seven yards.
news.head: Josh Downs snags four passes in loss
news.impact: Downs once again had a healthy target share, but didn't have a big day, even with Tyler Warren missing the game. Keenan Allen seemed to be the primary beneficiary of Warren's absence. Downs will need to show fantasy managers he can do more to be worth starting in lineups on a regular basis.

news.body: Josh Downs (hamstring) is good to go for Sunday's game against the Tennessee Titans.
news.head: Josh Downs (hamstring) good to go for Sunday
news.impact: Downs will be available to play on Sunday, despite popping up on Indianapolis' injury report earlier in the week with a hamstring issue. Look for him to see a large portion of Indianapolis' passing work against the Titans on Sunday, especially if Tyler Warren (groin) is ruled out.

news.body: Josh Downs (rest/hamstring) was limited at practice on Wednesday.
news.head: Josh Downs (rest/hamstring) limited at practice Wednesday
news.impact: The young wideout was able to practice on Wednesday, though he's dealing with some kind of a hamstring injury and was limited as a result. It looks like he's trending towards playing in Week 6, but we won't know his official status until later on in the week.

news.body: Josh Downs caught three of six targets for 47 yards in the Colts' 34-22 loss to the Steelers on Sunday.
news.head: Josh Downs goes for 47 yards in loss
news.impact: Downs had a couple of chances to make his day a little more palatable, but failed to make a catch in some tightly contested spots. Why Downs was targeted fewer times than Laquon Treadwell, who had less success, is a mystery. If it's any comfort, Downs looked to be regularly open and beating his man; Jones was just not finding him.

news.body: Justin Jefferson hauled in six of his seven targets for a team-leading 79 yards and one touchdown in the Vikings' 23-13 Week 5 win over the New Orleans Saints.
news.head: Justin Jefferson finds end zone in Week 5 win over Saints
news.impact: Jefferson has offered mixed results in the Minnesota passing attack to begin the season, reaching the end zone in two of his four contests. The wideout enters the Week 6 bye as one of many inconsistent offensive options for head coach Kevin O'Connell.

news.body: Justin Jefferson (ankle) is officially active for the Minnesota Vikings against the New Orleans Saints according to Tom Pelissero.
news.head: Justin Jefferson (ankle) active for Week 5
news.impact: Jefferson is good to go after not experiencing any issues in pregame activities for head coach Kevin O’Connell, and is is in line for a sizeable workload with Jordan Addison sidelined against the Saints.

news.body: Justin Jefferson (ankle) is expected to play for the Minnesota Vikings against the New Orleans Saints Sunday according to Jeff Darlington.
news.head: Justin Jefferson (ankle) expected to play Sunday
